name: Asteraceae
tip: What looks like one flower is a head of many tiny florets, often with strap-shaped rays round the edge and a ring of green bracts beneath. Dandelions, thistles, daisies, ragworts.

name: Rosaceae
tip: Usually 5 separate petals, many stamens and leafy stipules at the base of the leaf stalk; fruits often fleshy (hips, haws, brambles, cherries).

name: Poaceae
tip: Round, usually hollow stems with solid joints; long narrow leaves with a sheath wrapping the stem and a small flap (ligule) where blade meets sheath. Flowers in tiny green spikelets.

name: Fabaceae
tip: Pea-flowers: a large upper petal, two side wings and a boat-shaped keel. Leaves usually compound, often with tendrils; fruit a pod.

name: Cyperaceae
tip: Grass-like, but stems usually solid and triangular ('sedges have edges'); leaves in three ranks with no ligule flap. Cotton-grasses and spike-rushes belong here too.

name: Brassicaceae
tip: Four petals in a cross, six stamens (four long, two short); fruit a pod that splits from the bottom, leaving a papery central wall. Often a cress-like taste.

name: Caryophyllaceae
tip: Leaves in opposite pairs on stems swollen at the joints; five petals, often notched or deeply split (stitchworts, campions, chickweeds).

name: Apiaceae
tip: Tiny flowers in umbrella-shaped clusters (umbels), usually white; leaves often finely divided with a sheathing base; stems often hollow and ridged. Some are very poisonous.

name: Lamiaceae
tip: Square stems, opposite leaves, two-lipped flowers in rings up the stem; many smell when crushed (mints, dead-nettles, thymes).

name: Plantaginaceae
tip: A mixed family: plantains (ribbed leaves, brown flower spikes), speedwells (4 blue petals, 2 stamens), foxglove, toadflaxes, water-starworts.

name: Ranunculaceae
tip: Many stamens and separate petals or petal-like sepals; leaves often deeply lobed; fruit a cluster of small dry seeds. Buttercups, anemones, columbines, Clematis.

name: Orchidaceae
tip: Six petal-like parts, the lowest forming a distinctive lip, often patterned or spurred; leaves with parallel veins, sometimes spotted.

name: Polygonaceae
tip: A papery sheath (ochrea) round the stem above each leaf base; small flowers, 3 to 6 parts; fruit a 3-sided nut. Docks, sorrels, knotweeds, bistorts.

name: Amaranthaceae
tip: Small green flowers in dense clusters; leaves often mealy or fleshy; plants of bare and salty ground (goosefoots, oraches, glassworts).

name: Boraginaceae
tip: Rough, bristly hairs; flowers in coiled sprays that unroll as they open, often turning from pink to blue (forget-me-nots, comfreys, borage).

name: Amaryllidaceae
tip: Six-petalled flowers from a papery sheath; leaves strap-like from a bulb. Onions and garlics (umbels, onion smell), daffodils (with a trumpet), snowdrops.

name: Orobanchaceae
tip: Semi-parasites (eyebright, yellow-rattle, cow-wheat, lousewort) with two-lipped flowers; broomrapes have no green at all.

name: Ericaceae
tip: Small evergreen shrubs with bell- or urn-shaped flowers; leaves often tiny, needle-like or leathery (heathers, bilberry, rhododendron).

name: Juncaceae
tip: Grass-like; rushes have round stems, often filled with white pith; woodrushes have flat, hairy-edged leaves. Flowers small, brown, six-parted.

name: Iridaceae
tip: Sword-shaped leaves in a flat fan; showy flowers with 6 parts and 3 stamens (irises, crocuses, montbretia).

name: Asparagaceae
tip: Bulb or rhizome plants with parallel-veined leaves and six-parted flowers: bluebell, lily-of-the-valley, Solomon's-seal, butcher's-broom.

name: Geraniaceae
tip: Five separate petals and a long beak-like fruit (the 'crane's bill'); leaves usually lobed like a hand or finely divided.

name: Campanulaceae
tip: Bell-shaped, usually blue flowers; milky sap; ovary below the flower (harebell, bellflowers, sheep's-bit).

name: Primulaceae
tip: Five petals joined at the base, with the stamens opposite the petal lobes (primroses, cowslips, loosestrifes, scarlet pimpernel).

name: Crassulaceae
tip: Thick, fleshy, water-storing leaves; star-shaped flowers. Walls, rocks and dry places (stonecrops, houseleek, navelwort).

name: Caprifoliaceae
tip: Opposite leaves; includes honeysuckle, teasels and scabiouses (flower heads), valerians and snowberry.

name: Aspleniaceae
tip: Ferns: no flowers; fronds uncurl from a crozier and carry spore patches underneath. Spleenworts, lady-fern, hard-fern, bladder-ferns.

name: Papaveraceae
tip: Poppies: 4 crumpled petals, many stamens, often milky or coloured sap. Fumitories and corydalis have small tubular, spurred flowers.

name: Saxifragaceae
tip: Small plants of rocks, mountains and damp places; five petals, often white; leaves frequently in a basal rosette. Golden-saxifrages have no petals.

name: Potamogetonaceae
tip: Water plants with floating or submerged leaves and small green flower spikes held above the water.

name: Onagraceae
tip: Four petals and a long, thin ovary below the flower; seeds often with silky hairs (willowherbs, evening-primroses, enchanter's-nightshade has 2 petals).

name: Salicaceae
tip: Trees and shrubs with catkins, male and female on separate plants; seeds with cottony hairs.

name: Rubiaceae
tip: Leaves in whorls (rings) of 4 to 12 round square stems; tiny 4-petalled flowers. Cleavers is the sticky one.

name: Polypodiaceae
tip: Ferns: no flowers. Buckler-ferns, male-fern, shield-ferns and polypodies, with round spore patches on the frond underside.

name: Hypericaceae
tip: Opposite leaves, often with see-through dots when held up to the light; yellow flowers with many stamens in bundles.

name: Euphorbiaceae
tip: Spurges have milky sap and odd cup-like green flower clusters with no petals; dog's mercury has small green flowers on spikes.

name: Plumbaginaceae
tip: Coastal plants with leaves in a basal rosette; pink or lavender flowers with papery calyces (thrift heads, sea-lavender sprays).

name: Gentianaceae
tip: Hairless plants with opposite leaves and petals joined into a tube with 4 to 5 spreading lobes (centauries, gentians, yellow-wort).

name: Scrophulariaceae
tip: Figworts have square stems and small brown two-lipped flowers; mulleins have tall spikes of yellow flowers and often woolly leaves. Buddleja belongs here.

name: Araceae
tip: Lords-and-ladies: a hooded leaf-like spathe round a club-shaped spike, then red berries. Duckweeds (tiny floating green discs) are in this family too.

name: Oxalidaceae
tip: Clover-like leaves of three heart-shaped leaflets that fold down at night; five petals; sharp-tasting.

name: Solanaceae
tip: Five petals joined into a star or bell, with stamens forming a cone in the centre; fruit a berry or capsule. Many poisonous (bittersweet, deadly nightshade, henbane).

name: Violaceae
tip: Five unequal petals, the lowest with a backward spur; leaves often heart-shaped (violets and pansies).

name: Aizoaceae
tip: Introduced succulents with thick, three-sided or cylindrical leaves and large daisy-like flowers with many narrow petals; coastal cliffs.

name: Malvaceae
tip: Mallows: five notched petals and a central column of stamens; fruit like a round cheese. Limes are trees with a strap-like bract on the flower stalk.

name: Hydrocharitaceae
tip: Water plants: frogbit (floating, kidney-shaped leaves, 3 white petals), water-soldier, and the submerged waterweeds with whorled leaves.

name: Alismataceae
tip: Wetland plants with long-stalked basal leaves and flowers with 3 white or pale pink petals (water-plantains, arrowhead).

name: Araliaceae
tip: Ivy: evergreen climber with lobed leaves on climbing stems and ball-shaped umbels of greenish flowers in autumn. Marsh pennywort has round, umbrella-like leaves.

name: Lentibulariaceae
tip: Insect-catching plants: butterworts have sticky, pale green leaf rosettes; bladderworts float in water with tiny bladder traps.

name: Betulaceae
tip: Trees and shrubs with catkins in late winter or spring; fruits are nuts (hazel), tiny winged seeds (birch) or woody 'cones' (alder).

name: Pinaceae
tip: Conifers with needles (single, in pairs or in bunches) and woody cones (pines, spruces, firs, larch).

name: Liliaceae
tip: Bulb plants with large six-petalled flowers and parallel-veined leaves (fritillary, tulips, lilies, yellow star-of-Bethlehem).

name: Equisetaceae
tip: No flowers; jointed, ridged stems with rings of tiny teeth and whorls of thin green branches; spores in a cone at the stem tip.

name: Viburnaceae
tip: Shrubs with opposite leaves and flat-topped clusters of small white flowers, then berries (elder, guelder-rose, wayfaring-tree). Moschatel is a small herb.

name: Asphodelaceae
tip: Mostly introduced: New Zealand flax (huge leathery sword leaves), red-hot pokers, day-lilies; six-parted flowers.

name: Typhaceae
tip: Tall water-edge plants with long flat leaves: bulrushes have brown sausage-shaped heads; bur-reeds have spiky green balls.

name: Convolvulaceae
tip: Twining climbers with funnel-shaped flowers and arrow-shaped leaves. Dodders are leafless pink threads with no green.

name: Fagaceae
tip: Trees with catkins; fruit a nut in a cup or husk (acorns, beech-mast, sweet chestnuts).

name: Oleaceae
tip: Opposite leaves; flowers with 4 joined petals and 2 stamens, or no petals in ash. Ash has winged 'keys'; privet has black berries.

name: Sapindaceae
tip: Trees with opposite leaves: maples and sycamore have lobed leaves and paired winged fruits; horse-chestnut has hand-like compound leaves and conkers.

name: Urticaceae
tip: Small green flowers in dangling tassels; stinging nettle has stinging hairs, pellitory-of-the-wall does not.

name: Lycopodiaceae
tip: No flowers; creeping or upright stems densely covered in small, narrow, overlapping leaves; spores in cones or leaf bases.

name: Grossulariaceae
tip: Shrubs with lobed, maple-like leaves and hanging sprays of small flowers, then berries (currants, gooseberry, which is spiny).

name: Cistaceae
tip: Low, often woody-based plants of dry grassland with crumpled, short-lived yellow petals and many stamens.

name: Haloragaceae
tip: Submerged water plants with feathery leaves in whorls; small flowers on spikes above the water.

name: Linaceae
tip: Slender plants with narrow, untoothed leaves and 5 separate petals that drop quickly (fairy flax is white, flax blue).

name: Cornaceae
tip: Opposite leaves whose veins curve round towards the tip; 4-petalled flowers in flat clusters; dogwood has red winter stems.

name: Ulmaceae
tip: Trees with rough, toothed leaves that are lopsided at the base; fruit a flat papery wing round a seed.

name: Ophioglossaceae
tip: Small ferns with a single leaf and a separate spore-bearing spike or branch.

name: Cupressaceae
tip: Conifers with tiny scale-like or short prickly leaves; juniper has blue-black berry-like cones.

name: Aristolochiaceae
tip: Introduced woodland plants with heart- or kidney-shaped leaves and odd tubular or cup-shaped brownish flowers.

name: Montiaceae
tip: Small, fleshy, hairless plants with 5 white or pink petals; spring-beauty has a leaf collar round the stem below the flowers.

name: Resedaceae
tip: Spikes of small yellowish flowers with deeply cut petals and many stamens (weld, wild mignonette); bare chalky ground.

name: Pteridaceae
tip: Ferns: no flowers. Maidenhair fern has black stalks and fan-shaped leaflets; parsley fern grows in upland screes.

name: Nymphaeaceae
tip: Large round floating leaves with a slit to the centre; big white or yellow flowers floating or held just above the water.

name: Berberidaceae
tip: Spiny shrubs with yellow flowers and berries; Oregon-grape has holly-like compound leaves.

name: Vitaceae
tip: Woody climbers with tendrils; Virginia-creeper has hand-like leaves that turn red; small greenish flowers, then berries.

name: Polygalaceae
tip: Small plants of grassland and heath with blue, pink or white flowers: two large petal-like side sepals and a fringed lower petal.

name: Balsaminaceae
tip: Succulent stems; hooded, spurred flowers; seed pods that explode when touched (Himalayan balsam, touch-me-not).

name: Acanthaceae
tip: Introduced: large glossy, deeply lobed leaves and tall spikes of hooded flowers under spiny purple bracts.

name: Droseraceae
tip: Small bog plants with rosettes of round or narrow leaves covered in sticky red hairs that trap insects.

name: Isoetaceae
tip: No flowers; underwater rosettes of stiff, quill-like leaves at the bottom of clear lakes; spores at the leaf bases.

name: Lythraceae
tip: Purple-loosestrife: tall spikes of magenta flowers with 6 crinkled petals by water. Water-purslane is small and creeping.

name: Apocynaceae
tip: Trailing evergreen periwinkles with glossy opposite leaves and blue flowers whose 5 petals look twisted like a propeller.

name: Anacardiaceae
tip: Introduced stag's-horn sumach: shrub with velvety shoots, long pinnate leaves that turn red, dense red fruit clusters.

name: Phrymaceae
tip: Waterside plants with opposite leaves and large yellow, two-lipped, snapdragon-like flowers, often red-spotted.

name: Rutaceae
tip: Introduced aromatic shrubs with gland-dotted leaves (Mexican orange-blossom, rue).

name: Rhamnaceae
tip: Shrubs with small greenish 4 to 5-parted flowers and black berries; buckthorn is thorny with opposite leaves, alder buckthorn is thornless.

name: Hymenophyllaceae
tip: Tiny ferns with translucent fronds one cell thick, on wet shaded rocks and tree trunks in the west.

name: Celastraceae
tip: Spindle: shrub with green stems and pink four-lobed fruits with orange seeds. Grass-of-Parnassus: white 5-petalled flowers with fringed glands, wet places.

name: Juglandaceae
tip: Introduced trees with large aromatic pinnate leaves and catkins; walnuts, wing-nuts.

name: Acoraceae
tip: Iris-like leaves that smell of tangerines when crushed; a green finger-like flower spike sticking out sideways from a leaf-like stem.

name: Menyanthaceae
tip: Water plants: bogbean has three-part leaves and fringed white-pink flowers; fringed water-lily has small round floating leaves and yellow flowers.

name: Dennstaedtiaceae
tip: Fern: no flowers. Bracken has tall, single, much-divided fronds rising from underground stems, often in large stands.

name: Thymelaeaceae
tip: Shrubs with leathery leaves crowded towards the shoot tips and scented four-lobed flowers, then poisonous berries (mezereon, spurge-laurel).

name: Santalaceae
tip: Mistletoe: evergreen ball of forked green stems in trees, white berries. Bastard-toadflax: small parasitic herb of chalk grassland.

name: Zosteraceae
tip: Marine plants: long, grass-like ribbon leaves on sandy and muddy shores below the tide line.

name: Myricaceae
tip: Low shrub of bogs with grey-green leaves that smell resinous when crushed; catkins in spring.

name: Elatinaceae
tip: Tiny creeping plants of lake edges and mud with opposite leaves and minute pinkish flowers.

name: Ceratophyllaceae
tip: Rootless submerged water plants with whorls of stiff, forked, finely toothed leaves.

name: Cannabaceae
tip: Hop: twining rough-stemmed climber with lobed leaves and papery, cone-like female flower heads.

name: Juncaginaceae
tip: Grass-like plants of salt marsh and wet ground with fleshy, narrow leaves and a long slender spike of tiny green flowers.

name: Elaeagnaceae
tip: Spiny shrub with narrow silvery leaves and bright orange berries, mostly on sand dunes.

name: Selaginellaceae
tip: Small moss-like plant with tiny pointed leaves, in wet upland grassland and flushes; no flowers.

name: Pittosporaceae
tip: Introduced evergreen shrubs or trees with glossy leaves and small dark purple scented flowers; south-west coasts.

name: Ruppiaceae
tip: Submerged plants of brackish pools with thread-like leaves; flowers on long stalks.

name: Myrtaceae
tip: Introduced evergreen shrubs with aromatic, gland-dotted opposite leaves, white flowers with many stamens and edible berries.

name: Nothofagaceae
tip: Introduced trees planted for forestry, similar to beech but with smaller leaves.

name: Verbenaceae
tip: Wiry plant with square stems, lobed opposite leaves and long thin spikes of tiny lilac flowers.

name: Sarraceniaceae
tip: Introduced to a few bogs: leaves form upright tubes (pitchers) that trap insects.

name: Aquifoliaceae
tip: Evergreen tree or shrub with glossy, usually spiny leaves, small white 4-petalled flowers and red berries.

name: Alstroemeriaceae
tip: Garden escape with twisted leaf stalks and showy streaked flowers with 6 tepals.

name: Melanthiaceae
tip: Woodland plant with a single ring of four broad leaves and one starry green flower, then a black berry.

name: Marsileaceae
tip: Tiny fern of pond margins with grass-like leaves that uncurl like a crozier and pea-sized spore pills at the base.

name: Limnanthaceae
tip: Garden escape (poached-egg plant): white petals with yellow centres and divided leaves.

name: Lauraceae
tip: Bay: evergreen tree or shrub with aromatic leathery leaves used in cooking.

name: Frankeniaceae
tip: Low, mat-forming plant of salt marshes with tiny inrolled leaves and small pink flowers.

name: Eriocaulaceae
tip: Western Scottish and Irish lakes: underwater rosettes of grass-like leaves and small white button-heads on leafless stalks above the water.

name: Gunneraceae
tip: Introduced: gigantic rhubarb-like leaves on prickly stalks, with a huge cone-like spike of tiny flowers.

name: Butomaceae
tip: Tall water-edge plant with three-angled leaves and an umbel of pink six-petalled flowers.

name: Cabombaceae
tip: Introduced aquarium plant: submerged fan-shaped, finely divided opposite leaves and small white flowers.

name: Buxaceae
tip: Evergreen shrub with small, glossy, oval opposite leaves and tiny greenish flowers; chalk slopes and gardens.

name: Calceolariaceae
tip: Introduced: pouched, slipper-shaped yellow two-lipped flowers.

name: Colchicaceae
tip: Pink crocus-like flowers in autumn without leaves; broad leaves appear in spring. Poisonous.

name: Cucurbitaceae
tip: Climber with coiled tendrils, rough lobed leaves, greenish-white flowers and red berries.

name: Diapensiaceae
tip: Very rare: cushion plant on one Scottish mountain, with white five-petalled flowers.

name: Dioscoreaceae
tip: Twining climber with glossy heart-shaped leaves, small greenish flowers and red berries; no tendrils.

name: Pontederiaceae
tip: Introduced water plants with glossy leaves and spikes of blue flowers.

name: Portulacaceae
tip: Fleshy, sprawling annual with small yellow flowers; a garden weed.

name: Polemoniaceae
tip: Ladder-like pinnate leaves and clusters of blue bell-shaped flowers; limestone in northern England.

name: Paulowniaceae
tip: Introduced tree with very large, soft, opposite leaves and upright clusters of violet foxglove-like flowers.

name: Phytolaccaceae
tip: Introduced tall plant with reddish stems, upright spikes of small flowers and dark purple berries.

name: Moraceae
tip: Introduced tree with heart-shaped, sometimes lobed leaves, milky sap and blackberry-like fruits.

name: Osmundaceae
tip: Large fern of wet places whose fertile fronds end in rusty-brown, flower-like spore clusters; no true flowers.

name: Paeoniaceae
tip: Garden escape with large red flowers and divided leaves.

name: Nartheciaceae
tip: Bog plant with flat, sword-shaped leaves and spikes of starry orange-yellow flowers.

name: Scheuchzeriaceae
tip: Very rare bog plant with grass-like leaves that have a pore at the tip, and a few yellowish-green flowers.

name: Salviniaceae
tip: Introduced tiny floating fern forming red or green carpets on still water; no flowers.

name: Saururaceae
tip: Introduced: heart-shaped leaves smelling of orange peel and spikes of tiny flowers with four white petal-like bracts.

name: Tropaeolaceae
tip: Garden escape with round, umbrella-like leaves and orange or yellow spurred flowers.

name: Tofieldiaceae
tip: Small northern plant of wet flushes with a fan of short flat leaves and a tight head of pale greenish-white flowers.

name: Simaroubaceae
tip: Introduced tree with very long pinnate leaves, unpleasant-smelling when crushed, and twisted winged fruits.

name: Cyatheaceae
tip: Introduced tree-fern (Dicksonia) with a fibrous trunk topped by large fronds; south-west gardens and woods.

name: Taxaceae
tip: Evergreen conifer with flat, dark green needles in two rows and red fleshy cups around single seeds; no cones. All parts except the red flesh are poisonous.

name: Lamium album
tip: Looks like a stinging nettle but has white flowers and does not sting.

name: Lamium purpureum
tip: Upper leaves crowded and tinged purple; an annual of gardens and bare ground.

name: Lamium amplexicaule
tip: Upper leaves have no stalk and clasp the stem in pairs beneath the flowers.

name: Lamium galeobdolon
tip: Yellow flowers with reddish streaks on the lower lip; an ancient-woodland indicator.

name: Glechoma hederacea
tip: Kidney-shaped, round-toothed leaves on long creeping stems; smells pungent when crushed.

name: Prunella vulgaris
tip: Dense, squarish flower head with purple-tinged bracts and a pair of leaves just below it. Common in lawns.

name: Stachys sylvatica
tip: Dark wine-red flowers with white markings; stinks when crushed.

name: Stachys palustris
tip: Paler pinkish-purple flowers than Hedge Woundwort; narrow leaves with little or no stalk.

name: Mentha aquatica
tip: Rounded lilac flower head at the stem tip; strong mint smell.

name: Mentha arvensis
tip: Flowers only in whorls up the stem; the stem ends in leaves, not flowers.

name: Thymus drucei
tip: Low mats of tiny leaves; stems hairy on two opposite sides only.

name: Origanum vulgare
tip: Loose, branched clusters with purple bracts; smells of oregano.

name: Teucrium scorodonia
tip: Pale greenish-yellow flowers with no upper lip; wrinkled, sage-like leaves; acid soils.

name: Ajuga reptans
tip: Glossy leaves, leafy runners and a very short upper lip.

name: Galeopsis tetrahit
tip: Bristly stem that swells just below each pair of leaves.

name: Ballota nigra
tip: Rank-smelling hedgerow plant; the calyx has broad, spreading teeth.

name: Clinopodium vulgare
tip: Flower whorls wrapped in long, bristly hairs, so they look woolly; only faintly aromatic.

name: Lycopus europaeus
tip: Deeply toothed to lobed leaves; tiny purple-dotted white flowers in tight whorls.

name: Scutellaria galericulata
tip: Flowers in pairs in the leaf axils, all facing one way; calyx has a small hump.

name: Betonica officinalis
tip: Rosette of long-stalked, oblong leaves; reddish-purple flowers in a dense spike.

name: Ranunculus repens
tip: Long runners that root at the joints; leaves with three leaflets, the middle one on its own stalk; flower stalks furrowed.

name: Ranunculus acris
tip: Tall and hairy with no runners; leaves deeply cut like a hand; flower stalks round and smooth, not furrowed.

name: Ficaria verna
tip: Early spring; glossy heart-shaped leaves; 8 to 12 narrow, shiny yellow petals; often small bulbils where the leaves join the stem.

name: Caltha palustris
tip: Large glossy kidney-shaped leaves; big golden cup flowers with no green sepals beneath; marshes and wet woods.

name: Ranunculus flammula
tip: Narrow, spear-shaped leaves and small yellow buttercup flowers; wet ground and pond edges.

name: Anemone nemorosa
tip: Spring carpets in old woods; a single white flower, often pink-tinged beneath, above a ring of three divided leaves.

name: Ranunculus bulbosus
tip: Sepals folded right back down the flower stalk; stem base swollen like a small bulb; dry grassland.

name: Aquilegia vulgaris
tip: Nodding flowers with five hooked spurs, usually violet-blue; leaves divided into rounded, lobed leaflets.

name: Ranunculus sceleratus
tip: Hairless, shiny, often hollow stem; tiny pale yellow flowers with a large green fruiting head in the middle; muddy pond edges.

name: Ranunculus hederaceus
tip: Small creeping plant of shallow water and mud with only ivy-shaped leaves (no thread-like ones) and tiny white flowers.

name: Clematis vitalba
tip: Woody climber over hedges and scrub on chalk and limestone; creamy flowers with 4 sepals; feathery 'old man's beard' seed heads.

name: Ranunculus auricomus
tip: Woodland buttercup whose petals are often missing or misshapen; rounded basal leaves, narrow finger-like stem leaves.

name: Helleborus foetidus
tip: Evergreen; dark leaves cut into narrow fingers; nodding pale green bells rimmed with purple in late winter.

name: Ranunculus lingua
tip: Tall water-edge plant with long narrow leaves and large (3 to 5 cm) yellow flowers.

name: Ranunculus aquatilis
tip: White flowers on the water; both floating lobed leaves and submerged thread-like leaves; ponds and ditches. Water-crowfoots are a tricky group: check with a specialist.

name: Thalictrum minus
tip: Finely divided leaves like maidenhair fern; loose sprays of small drooping greenish-yellow flowers that are mostly stamens. Dunes and limestone.

name: Ranunculus omiophyllus
tip: Like Ivy-leaved Crowfoot but leaves more deeply lobed and flowers larger; western, on acid mud and in streams.

name: Ranunculus trichophyllus
tip: Only short, submerged thread-like leaves that collapse out of water; small white flowers; ponds and ditches.

name: Trollius europaeus
tip: Large globe-shaped yellow flowers of incurved petals; damp upland meadows and streamsides in the north.

name: Ranunculus peltatus
tip: Floating rounded leaves plus thread-like submerged ones; large white flowers; ponds and slow water.

name: Ranunculus penicillatus
tip: Long trailing submerged threads in flowing rivers, sometimes with floating leaves; large white flowers.

name: Aconitum napellus
tip: Tall spikes of deep blue-violet hooded flowers; deeply cut hand-shaped leaves; shady streamsides. Very poisonous.

name: Thalictrum flavum
tip: Tall plant of fens and riversides with dense clusters of fluffy pale yellow stamens; leaves with many leaflets.

name: Ranunculus sardous
tip: Like Bulbous Buttercup (sepals bent back) but paler yellow, hairier and with no swollen stem base; damp ground, often near the coast.

name: Thalictrum alpinum
tip: Small mountain plant with a few drooping purplish flowers on a slender stalk; leaves with small rounded leaflets.

name: Ranunculus parviflorus
tip: Sprawling hairy annual with tiny yellow flowers and rounded, lobed leaves; seeds covered in hooked bumps.

name: Helleborus viridis
tip: Dies down in winter; flat, open green flowers in early spring; leaves cut into toothed fingers; woods on lime.

name: Ranunculus fluitans
tip: Very long, dark green, tassel-like submerged leaves in fast rivers; no floating leaves.

name: Ranunculus circinatus
tip: Stiff, flat, circular fans of short thread-like leaves that keep their shape when lifted out of water.

name: Ranunculus baudotii
tip: Water-crowfoot of brackish coastal ditches and pools; floating and thread-like leaves.

name: Myosurus minimus
tip: Tiny plant with grass-like leaves; the fruiting head stretches into a long, thin, mouse-tail spike.

name: Ranunculus arvensis
tip: Rare cornfield weed with pale yellow flowers and large seeds covered in sharp spines.

name: Ranunculus tripartitus
tip: Rare, south-west; tiny white flowers; deeply three-lobed floating leaves, sometimes thread-like ones too; seasonal pools.

name: Adonis annua
tip: Rare cornfield annual with feathery leaves and blood-red flowers with a dark centre.

name: Pulsatilla vulgaris
tip: Silky-hairy plant of chalk and limestone grassland with large purple bell flowers in spring, then feathery seed heads.

name: Actaea spicata
tip: Rare, in limestone woods and pavement in northern England; fluffy spikes of small white flowers, then black berries.

name: Ranunculus reptans
tip: Very rare; slender arching runners that root at each joint, with narrow leaves; stony lake shores.

name: Ranunculus ophioglossifolius
tip: Very rare; oval to heart-shaped lower leaves and small pale yellow flowers in muddy pools.

name: Eranthis hyemalis
tip: Garden escape in woods and parks; yellow cup flowers in mid-winter sitting on a ruff of deeply cut leaves.

name: Anemone blanda
tip: Garden escape; low plant with many narrow blue, pink or white petals in early spring.

name: Anemone apennina
tip: Garden escape like Wood Anemone but with sky-blue flowers of 10 to 15 narrow petals.

name: Helleborus argutifolius
tip: Garden escape with leathery evergreen leaves of three spiny-toothed leaflets and pale green cup flowers in winter.

name: Helleborus orientalis
tip: Garden escape; nodding cup flowers in late winter and spring, cream, pink or purple; leathery leaves.

name: Nigella damascena
tip: Garden escape; blue flowers in a ruff of thread-like bracts; swollen, balloon-like seed pods.

name: Consolida ajacis
tip: Garden escape; spikes of blue, pink or white flowers with one long spur; very finely divided leaves.

name: Alliaria petiolata
tip: Hedgerow and woodland-edge plant with heart-shaped toothed leaves that smell of garlic when crushed, and small white four-petalled flowers in spring.

name: Arabidopsis thaliana
tip: Tiny annual of dry bare ground and walls with a flat rosette of small leaves and a wiry stem of tiny white flowers and long thin pods.

name: Arabis hirsuta
tip: Upright, hairy plant of dry banks and walls with clasping stem leaves pressed to the stem and small white flowers; pods held upright and close.

name: Armoracia rusticana
tip: Tall, coarse plant of roadsides and waste ground with huge dock-like basal leaves, narrower lobed upper leaves and clusters of small white flowers.

name: Aubrieta deltoidea
tip: Low mat-forming garden escape on walls and rocks with grey-green leaves and bright purple to lilac four-petalled flowers in spring.

name: Barbarea intermedia
tip: Yellow-flowered winter-cress with smaller flowers than Winter-cress and slender pods; upper leaves are lobed, and the flower buds are not compact.

name: Barbarea vulgaris
tip: Shiny dark green leaves with a large rounded end lobe and smaller side lobes; yellow flowers with buds in a dense head, on damp ground and verges.

name: Brassica napus
tip: Blue-grey hairless leaves whose upper ones clasp the stem; open flowers sit level with or just above the buds in crop fields and verges.

name: Brassica nigra
tip: Tall, bristly plant of riverbanks and coasts with small yellow flowers and short pods pressed tight against the stem; lower leaves lobed and rough.

name: Brassica rapa
tip: Upper leaves clasp the stem with rounded basal lobes, grey-green and slightly waxy, and open flowers overtop the buds; found by rivers and on waste ground.

name: Cakile maritima
tip: Fleshy, lobed-leaved plant of sandy and shingle beaches with pale lilac to white flowers and short, swollen, two-segmented pods.

name: Capsella bursa-pastoris
tip: Common weed with tiny white flowers and flat heart-shaped or triangular pods like little purses; basal rosette of variably lobed leaves.

name: Cardamine amara
tip: Damp-ground bitter-cress with white flowers and distinctive purple anthers; stem is solid and leafy, with large flowers for the group.

name: Cardamine flexuosa
tip: Zigzag hairy stem with leaves on it; usually six stamens and a rosette of leaves; shady, damp ground and gardens, often taller than Hairy Bitter-cress.

name: Cardamine hirsuta
tip: Small annual weed of bare ground with a rosette of pinnate leaves and few stem leaves; usually four stamens; pods shoot out when ripe.

name: Cardamine pratensis
tip: Pale lilac or pink flowers in damp meadows in spring; pinnate leaves with rounded leaflets on lower stem, narrow ones above; also called Lady's Smock.

name: Cochlearia danica
tip: Small coastal and inland-roadside annual with ivy-shaped stalked basal leaves and clusters of small white to lilac flowers in early spring.

name: Cochlearia officinalis
tip: Fleshy, shiny, rounded to heart-shaped leaves in salt marshes and sea cliffs, with white flowers in dense clusters and rounded pods.

name: Diplotaxis muralis
tip: Yellow flowers with dark veins on walls and railway tracks; leaves lobed and mainly in a basal rosette, with a leafless-looking stem and strong smell.

name: Erophila verna
tip: Tiny spring annual of walls and dry banks with a rosette of small leaves, leafless stems and white petals split nearly to the base.

name: Erysimum cheiranthoides
tip: Annual of arable fields and waste ground with narrow toothed leaves, small pale yellow flowers and thin four-sided pods pressed up the stem.

name: Erysimum cheiri
tip: Fragrant yellow to orange-brown flowers on old walls and cliffs; narrow dark green leaves and a woody base distinguish it from other yellow crucifers.

name: Hesperis matronalis
tip: Tall garden escape with sweetly scented purple, lilac or white flowers in spring; unlike phlox it has four petals and long thin pods.

name: Hirschfeldia incana
tip: Grey-green, bristly plant of roadsides and waste ground with small pale yellow flowers, pods tight against the stem and a lobed lower leaf.

name: Lepidium campestre
tip: Hairy plant of dry grassland and field edges with arrow-shaped stem leaves clasping the stem, small cream flowers and rough heart-shaped pods.

name: Lepidium coronopus
tip: Flat mat on trampled ground and paths with deeply cut leaves and flower clusters opposite the leaves; pods wrinkled, flattened and not notched.

name: Lepidium didymum
tip: Strong-smelling annual weed with finely divided leaves, tiny flowers and notched twin-lobed pods; upright and finer than Swine-cress.

name: Lepidium draba
tip: Patch-forming perennial of roadsides with grey downy foliage, arrow-shaped clasping stem leaves and dense domed clusters of white flowers.

name: Lepidium heterophyllum
tip: Greyish perennial pepperwort of waste ground and walls with violet anthers on white flowers and oval, clasping upper leaves.

name: Lobularia maritima
tip: Low, tufted garden escape with grey narrow leaves and masses of small honey-scented white flowers on walls and paving, flowering for months.

name: Lunaria annua
tip: Garden escape with heart-shaped toothed leaves, purple or white flowers and, later, round papery silvery seed discs.

name: Nasturtium microphyllum
tip: Water-cress growing in streams with leaves turning bronze-purple in autumn; fruit narrow and in a single row of seeds per segment.

name: Nasturtium officinale
tip: Edible aquatic plant of streams and ditches with glossy dark pinnate leaves that stay green; fruit seeds in two rows.

name: Raphanus raphanistrum
tip: Yellow, white or lilac flowers with dark veins and long beaded pods constricted between seeds; bristly arable weed with lobed leaves.

name: Rorippa palustris
tip: Small pale yellow flowers on a branched plant of muddy edges with deeply lobed leaves; short plump pods are longer than their stalks.

name: Rorippa sylvestris
tip: Creeping roots and finely divided leaves on bare damp ground and roadsides; slender pods longer than stalk, flowers bright yellow.

name: Sinapis alba
tip: Bristly plant with yellow flowers, and beaked pods with stiff spreading hairs; leaves lobed like an oak and the long beak is a sword shape.

name: Sinapis arvensis
tip: Common arable weed with bright yellow flowers, rough bristly stems and leaves, and smooth pods with a short beak ending the pod.

name: Sisymbrium officinale
tip: Stiff, wiry plant with widely spreading branches and tiny pale yellow flowers; pods pressed close to the stem. Common on verges and wasteland.

name: Sisymbrium orientale
tip: Pale yellow flowers on a tall hairy annual of roadsides and waste land; very long thin pods held away from the stem, lobed leaves.

name: Thlaspi arvense
tip: Hairless annual of fields with arrow-shaped clasping leaves and round flat winged pods that look like discs, notched at the tip.

name: Anthyllis vulneraria
tip: Round heads of yellow, sometimes orange or red, flowers cupped by furry bracts, with silky pinnate leaves; grassland, cliffs and dunes.

name: Cytisus scoparius
tip: Green, angular-stemmed shrub with bright yellow pea flowers and small trifoliate leaves; lacks spines unlike gorse.

name: Laburnum anagyroides
tip: Small garden tree with trifoliate leaves and long hanging chains of yellow pea flowers; all parts are poisonous; often self-sown.

name: Lathyrus latifolius
tip: Climber with winged stems, two broad leaflets, tendrils and large bright pink flower clusters; garden escape on rough ground.

name: Lathyrus linifolius
tip: Slender plant of woods and heaths with no tendrils, pinnate leaves, and flowers turning from crimson to blue-green; stem is winged.

name: Lathyrus nissolia
tip: Looks like a grass until it flowers: leaves are narrow and unbranched, with small crimson flowers on long stalks, in rough grassland.

name: Lathyrus pratensis
tip: Yellow pea flowers in short spikes in grassland and verges; paired narrow pointed leaflets with a simple tendril and a pair of arrow-shaped stipules.

name: Lotus corniculatus
tip: Yellow flowers often with orange buds in heads of 2-6; five leaflets, solid stem and pods spreading like a bird's foot.

name: Lotus pedunculatus
tip: Taller than Common Bird's-foot-trefoil with hollow stems, wetter habitats and heads of 5-12 flowers, blue-green leaflets and flowers reddish in bud.

name: Medicago arabica
tip: Clover-like leaves with a dark central blotch and small yellow flowers in clusters of 1-5; coiled spiny pods; lawns and dry ground.

name: Medicago lupulina
tip: Low yellow clover-like plant with small round flower heads and kidney-shaped black pods, leaflets with a tiny point on the tip.

name: Medicago sativa
tip: Purple flower clusters in tall oblong spikes with clover-like leaves on field edges; pods coiled like small springs.

name: Melilotus albus
tip: Tall plant with long spikes of small white flowers and trifoliate toothed leaves; smells of new hay; waste ground and roadsides.

name: Melilotus altissimus
tip: Yellow-flowered melilot with hairy, downy pods and wings and keel of equal length; keel equals standard, pods black when ripe.

name: Melilotus officinalis
tip: Yellow melilot with hairless, transversely ribbed pods that are brown when ripe; wings longer than keel; roadsides and waste ground.

name: Onobrychis viciifolia
tip: Dense spikes of pink veined flowers on chalk grassland and verges; leaves pinnate with many narrow leaflets, no tendrils.

name: Ononis repens
tip: Low, spreading, hairy, sticky plant with pink pea flowers and small toothed trifoliate leaves; unlike Spiny Restharrow it has no spines.

name: Ornithopus perpusillus
tip: Small, hairy annual of sandy heaths with tiny pinkish-white flowers in clusters and feathery pinnate leaves; pods curved like bird claws.

name: Robinia pseudoacacia
tip: Tree with deeply furrowed bark, pinnate leaves and hanging scented white pea flowers in spring; twigs bear short paired thorns.

name: Trifolium arvense
tip: Soft grey-pink furry cylindrical heads with fluffy sepals; low annual on sandy ground and dunes, with narrow trifoliate leaves.

name: Trifolium campestre
tip: Yellow clover with globular heads of 20-40 flowers turning brown like hops; central leaflet has a longer stalk than the side leaflets.

name: Trifolium dubium
tip: Smallest yellow clover, with heads of only 3-15 flowers; central leaflet is only slightly stalked. Common in lawns and grassland.

name: Trifolium hybridum
tip: Pink and white flower heads fading brown, with stalked heads and leaflets lacking a white mark; stems are not creeping; roadsides and fields.

name: Trifolium medium
tip: Zigzag stems, reddish-purple flowers in heads and leaflets with narrow pale markings, often in grassland and woodland margins.

name: Trifolium micranthum
tip: Very small, slender yellow clover with heads of 2-6 tiny flowers and an unstalked-looking central leaflet; short grassland, often on sandy soil.

name: Trifolium pratense
tip: Pink-purple rounded heads in meadows, leaflets with a pale crescent mark and hairy stipules, stems upright.

name: Trifolium repens
tip: Creeping stems that root at the nodes, round white flower heads and leaflets with a pale V mark; abundant in lawns and pastures.

name: Trifolium striatum
tip: Small pink clover on dry grassland with stalkless heads in the leaf axils and hairy, furrowed striped leaves, and short oval heads.

name: Ulex europaeus
tip: Dense spiny evergreen shrub with coconut-scented bright yellow flowers; spines are strong and furrowed; flowers on and off all year.

name: Ulex gallii
tip: Smaller, more compact gorse of western heaths and cliffs; flowers late summer to autumn, with short bracteoles and spines weaker than Gorse.

name: Vicia cracca
tip: Climbing, one-sided spikes of many blue-violet flowers and pinnate leaves with branched tendrils; hedgerows and grassland.

name: Vicia faba
tip: Upright, square stem with no tendrils, large white flowers with black blotches and thick pods; a crop escape.

name: Vicia sativa
tip: Pink-purple flowers singly or in pairs at the leaf bases, with a black spot on the stipule; leaflets vary from narrow to oval.

name: Vicia sepium
tip: Branched tendrils and two to six dull purple flowers in short-stalked clusters; leaflets oval; hedges, woodland edges and rough grassland.

name: Alnus cordata
tip: Planted tree with glossy, heart-shaped leaves and cone-like fruits; rounder leaves than Alder; catkins appear in late winter.

name: Alnus glutinosa
tip: Wet-ground tree with rounded leaves with a notched tip, small woody cone-like fruits and purple-brown male catkins in late winter.

name: Alnus incana
tip: Tree with pointed grey-green oval leaves, downy beneath, and catkins in winter; leaves sharper than Alder, with no notch at the tip.

name: Betula pendula
tip: White papery bark with black diamond marks, hairless twigs and drooping branches; leaves double-toothed and triangular.

name: Betula pubescens
tip: Birch with hairy young twigs, whiter bark without deep fissures and oval leaves with rounded base; wet heaths and moorland.

name: Carpinus betulus
tip: Tree with fluted grey trunk and oval leaves with parallel pleated veins, double-toothed; fruit has three-lobed bracts.

name: Corylus avellana
tip: Shrub with rounded, softly hairy toothed leaves; dangling yellow male catkins appear in late winter, tiny red female flowers.

name: Antirrhinum majus
tip: Garden escape on old walls and rubbly ground; large two-lipped flowers closed by a pouting lower lip, unlike the toadflaxes with spurs. Colours vary from pink to white or yellow.

name: Callitriche brutia
tip: Tiny aquatic or mud-dwelling plant with starry leaf rosettes; fruits sit on distinct stalks, unlike other water-starworts whose fruits are stalkless. Often on seasonally drying pools and ditches.

name: Callitriche platycarpa
tip: Water-starwort with floating rosettes of rounded leaves; fruits are stalkless and winged at the top, with spreading styles. Common in ponds and ditches, often with Common Water-starwort.

name: Callitriche stagnalis
tip: Most frequent water-starwort; floating rosettes of broad rounded leaves and stalkless fruits that are broadly winged, with a clearly keeled edge. Ponds, ditches and wet mud.

name: Chaenorhinum minus
tip: Small, sticky-hairy annual of arable fields and railway ballast; tiny pale purple flowers with a short spur, much smaller than Common Toadflax and with no yellow.

name: Cymbalaria muralis
tip: Trailing plant hanging from walls with fleshy ivy-shaped leaves; small lilac flowers with a yellow patch and a short spur. Common on old walls and pavements.

name: Digitalis purpurea
tip: Tall spike of nodding, tubular purple-pink flowers spotted inside, above a rosette of large downy leaves. Woodland clearings, heaths and banks; the only large tubular purple spire in this family.

name: Hippuris vulgaris
tip: Aquatic plant with erect stems bearing whorls of narrow leaves like tiny pines; flowers are minute and green in leaf axils. Not related to horsetail; grows in shallow still or slow water.

name: Kickxia elatine
tip: Trailing annual of arable fields with arrow-shaped leaves with two spreading basal lobes; flowers have a purple upper lip and yellow lower lip. Stalks hairless. Compare Round-leaved Fluellen.

name: Kickxia spuria
tip: Trailing annual of arable fields with rounded to oval leaves lacking basal lobes; flower stalks are hairy and the flowers have a deep purple upper lip and yellow lower lip.

name: Linaria purpurea
tip: Garden escape on walls and waste ground; tall, grey-green and slender with spikes of small violet-purple spurred flowers. Plants with pink forms occur; Common Toadflax is yellow.

name: Linaria vulgaris
tip: Spikes of yellow snapdragon-like flowers with an orange patch and long spur; narrow grey-green leaves crowded up the stem. Grassy banks, verges and hedgerows.

name: Littorella uniflora
tip: Small tufted plant of lake shores with narrow, pointed, quill-like leaves in a low mat; flowers inconspicuous on short stalks. Resembles a tiny plantain but grows on gravelly or muddy margins.

name: Plantago coronopus
tip: Flat rosette of narrow leaves cut into toothed lobes like antlers, with curved stalks and slender spikes. Coastal turf, sandy and gravelly places; also inland on dry gravel.

name: Plantago lanceolata
tip: Narrow ribbed leaves in a rosette, and a short dark brown head with a ring of white stamens on a long furrowed stalk. Very common in grassland and lawns.

name: Plantago major
tip: Broad oval leaves with five to nine strong veins and a long rat-tail spike of tiny greenish flowers. Common on paths, gateways and trampled ground.

name: Plantago maritima
tip: Rosette of narrow, fleshy, slightly toothed or smooth leaves on salt marshes, sea cliffs and mountain rocks; stiff narrow spikes. Distinguished from Ribwort by its fleshy leaves and coastal habitat.

name: Plantago media
tip: Broad downy oval leaves pressed flat in a rosette; fragrant lilac-pink stamens in a short head on a long stalk. Calcareous grassland and lawns.

name: Veronica agrestis
tip: Small sprawling annual of arable fields with pale blue flowers, the lowest petal white; individual flower stalks are shorter than the leaf, and the sepals are unequal. Comparable to Grey Field-speedwell.

name: Veronica anagallis-aquatica
tip: Stout hairless water-edge speedwell with stalkless, clasping, pointed leaves and many pale blue-violet flower spikes. Compare Pink Water-speedwell with narrower leaves and pink flowers; Brooklime has stalked leaves.

name: Veronica arvensis
tip: Small, hairy annual with tiny blue flowers in leafy spikes; upper leaves are small and bract-like. Found on walls, paths and cultivated land; flowers are smaller than those of Germander Speedwell.

name: Veronica beccabunga
tip: Fleshy, shiny rounded leaves with short stalks and loose spikes of bright blue flowers from the leaf axils. Streams, ditches and wet muddy ground.

name: Veronica catenata
tip: Water-edge speedwell with narrower, pointed stalkless leaves than Brooklime and pale pink veined flowers in spikes. Compare Blue Water-speedwell, which has bluer flowers and broader leaves.

name: Veronica chamaedrys
tip: Bright blue flowers with a white eye, with two distinctive hairy lines on the stem. Common on grassy verges, hedgebanks and woodland edges, the commonest speedwell of banks.

name: Veronica filiformis
tip: Creeping, mat-forming plant with pale blue single flowers on long thin stalks, forming dense lawn patches; leaves small and kidney-shaped. Non-native, spreads in lawns and grassland.

name: Veronica hederifolia
tip: Small annual with pale lilac-blue flowers and ivy-like leaves with a few large pointed lobes. Flowers early in the year in hedgebanks, gardens and arable fields.

name: Veronica montana
tip: Woodland speedwell with oval, stalked, toothed leaves and pale lilac flowers on long thin stalks; the stem is hairy all round. Ancient woods and damp shady banks.

name: Veronica officinalis
tip: Mat-forming hairy plant with rounded leaves and dense spikes of pale lilac flowers. Heaths, dry grassland and woodland edges, on acid soil.

name: Veronica persica
tip: Large bright blue flowers, the lowest petal paler, on long stalks; leaves are hairy and strongly toothed. Very common weed of gardens and arable fields, flowering most of the year.

name: Veronica polita
tip: Annual weed with bright blue flowers that have a short corolla; leaves are greyish and hairy. Smaller than Common Field-speedwell, with sepals that are broad and overlapping.

name: Veronica scutellata
tip: Slender creeping plant of marshy ground with narrow, lance-shaped leaves and few-flowered spikes of pale lilac-white flowers; seed capsules are notched. Bog margins and wet places.

name: Veronica serpyllifolia
tip: Creeping, rooting stems and small rounded smooth leaves; white or very pale blue flowers with darker veins in terminal spikes. Lawns, paths and heaths.

name: Agrostemma githago
tip: Tall slender plant with silky grey hairs and large purple-pink flowers with long narrow sepals extending beyond the petals. Now rare cornfield annual, occasional from seed mixes.

name: Arenaria leptoclados
tip: Slender annual like Thyme-leaved Sandwort but with a longer, narrower capsule and smaller seeds; found on dry open ground and walls. Best told by a lens.

name: Arenaria serpyllifolia
tip: Wiry, much-branched annual with small hairy oval pointed leaves and tiny white flowers with petals shorter than sepals. Common on dry bare ground, walls and sandy soil.

name: Cerastium diffusum
tip: Small coastal annual with tiny flowers, bracts leafy and bracts without membranous margins in tufts. Bears five stamens and four petals; found on sand and dunes.

name: Cerastium fontanum
tip: Perennial with hairy oval leaves, flowers with white notched petals about as long as sepals and sparse inflorescence. Common in grassland and lawns; a perennial, unlike the annual species.

name: Cerastium glomeratum
tip: Annual, sticky and hairy, with compact flower clusters of five-petalled white flowers with petals about equal to sepals. Waste ground, paths and arable fields.

name: Cerastium semidecandrum
tip: Tiny, early-flowering annual of dry sandy places with sepals having broad papery margins and petals that are small. Flowers disappear by early summer.

name: Cerastium tomentosum
tip: Garden escape forming silvery-white woolly mats with narrow leaves and masses of larger white flowers. Walls, banks and waste ground.

name: Honckenya peploides
tip: Fleshy, yellowish-green creeping plant on shingle and sand, with pairs of thick oval leaves and small greenish-white flowers. Strandline species.

name: Moehringia trinervia
tip: Woodland plant with oval leaves showing three clear veins and small white flowers with petals shorter than sepals. Weak straggling stems in shady, damp woods.

name: Sagina apetala
tip: Tiny annual with narrow leaves and four-parted flowers; petals are minute or absent and the sepals are pressed close to the capsule. Bare gravelly and sandy ground.

name: Sagina maritima
tip: Fleshy small pearlwort of coastal turf and salt-affected paths; capsule-pressed sepals, petals very small or absent, and fleshy blunt leaves. Annual of the coast.

name: Sagina nodosa
tip: Perennial pearlwort with little leaf clusters along the stem like knots, and white flowers larger than most pearlworts. Damp sandy ground and dune slacks.

name: Sagina procumbens
tip: Common mat-forming pearlwort in paths and lawns, with four-petalled flowers with minute petals and a central rosette; sepals spread out in fruit.

name: Saponaria officinalis
tip: Tall perennial with clustered pale pink five-petalled flowers and oval leaves with three to five veins. Hedgebanks, roadsides and waste ground, often a garden escape.

name: Silene coronaria
tip: Garden escape with felted silvery-white stems and leaves and bright magenta flowers. The dense white wool makes it unmistakable among campions.

name: Silene dioica
tip: Pink-red flowers with five notched petals, hairy stems and leaves, on woodland edges and hedgerows. Male and female flowers occur on separate plants; compare White Campion.

name: Silene flos-cuculi
tip: Pink flowers with each petal cut into four narrow lobes giving a tattered look. Wet meadows and fens, with narrow leaves and sparsely hairy stems.

name: Silene latifolia
tip: White flowers with five notched petals and sticky hairy stems and leaves, opening in the evening. Arable edges and hedgebanks; compare with Bladder Campion with its inflated calyx.

name: Silene uniflora
tip: Mat-forming plant with inflated white-veined calyx, white notched petals and fleshy grey-green leaves. Coastal cliffs and shingle, also mountain rocks.

name: Silene vulgaris
tip: Hairless blue-green plant with an inflated veined calyx like a bladder, and white deeply notched petals. Grassy places and roadsides.

name: Spergula arvensis
tip: Annual with thread-like whorled leaves and tiny white five-petalled flowers on sticky stalks. Light arable soils and disturbed sandy ground.

name: Spergularia marina
tip: Fleshy annual of salt marshes with narrow leaves and small pink flowers with whitish centres; petals shorter than sepals. Seeds without wing.

name: Spergularia media
tip: Perennial sea-spurrey with fleshy leaves and larger, pale pink flowers with white centres; petals longer than the sepals. Salt marshes and estuaries.

name: Spergularia rubra
tip: Small, spreading annual or biennial with thread-like leaves and pink flowers, silvery stipules and sticky hairy capsules. Sandy heaths and tracks, away from salt.

name: Stellaria alsine
tip: Slender stitchwort of wet places with oval leaves and tiny white flowers with petals shorter than the sepals, deeply cut. Streams, springs and flushes.

name: Stellaria graminea
tip: Slender, grass-like stitchwort with narrow, smooth leaves and loose, branched clusters of small white flowers (petals cleft almost to the base). Grassy banks, heaths and roadsides.

name: Stellaria holostea
tip: Large white star-like flowers with petals cleft halfway, on brittle square stems with rough narrow leaves. Hedgebanks and woodland edges in spring.

name: Stellaria media
tip: Sprawling plant with a single line of hairs on the stem and tiny white flowers with deeply cleft petals. Ubiquitous weed in gardens and arable land.

name: Stellaria neglecta
tip: Chickweed of damp shady places, larger and more robust than Common Chickweed, with ten stamens and larger petals; mostly in woods and by streams.

name: Stellaria pallida
tip: Tiny pale chickweed of sandy ground with minute or absent petals and few stamens. Flowers early, in sandy, coastal or disturbed places.

name: Amsinckia micrantha
tip: Rough bristly annual with one-sided coiled spikes of tiny yellow flowers. Alien weed of arable land, waste ground and sandy places.

name: Borago officinalis
tip: Bristly plant with bright blue starry flowers having a dark central cone. Garden escape on tips and waste ground; unlike other blue borages by its star shape.

name: Echium vulgare
tip: Bristly plant with spikes of funnel-shaped flowers, pink in bud turning bright blue, with protruding red stamens. Dry grassland, dunes and chalk.

name: Myosotis arvensis
tip: Hairy forget-me-not with small blue flowers and a calyx covered in hooked hairs, with style shorter than calyx. Arable land and open ground.

name: Myosotis discolor
tip: Tiny flowers that change from cream or yellow to blue as they age, within a coiled spike; calyx with hooked hairs. Dry sandy grassland and fields.

name: Myosotis laxa
tip: Forget-me-not of wet places with tiny pale blue flowers, with open calyx without hooked hairs, and fruit stalks longer than calyx. Compare Water Forget-me-not.

name: Myosotis ramosissima
tip: Tiny early-flowering annual with sky-blue flowers on short stalks, and calyx with hooked hairs. Dry open ground, flowering from early spring.

name: Myosotis scorpioides
tip: Stems rooting in wet places, flowers sky-blue with yellow eye, calyx with short teeth. Stream sides, ditches and marshes; larger flowers than other wet-place forget-me-nots.

name: Myosotis secunda
tip: Perennial of wet, acidic, upland places, creeping with rooting stems and bright blue flowers; calyx with open lobes in fruit. Streams and flushes.

name: Myosotis sylvatica
tip: Larger flowers in woods than other forget-me-nots, bright blue with a yellow centre, on hairy stems; calyx with hooked hairs. Woodland and garden escapes.

name: Pentaglottis sempervirens
tip: Large bristly perennial with bright blue flowers with white centres and big dark green oval leaves. Hedgebanks and roadsides, naturalised from gardens.

name: Phacelia tanacetifolia
tip: Tall annual with feathery deeply cut leaves and dense coiled spikes of lilac-blue flowers with protruding stamens, loved by bees. Sown as green manure and field margins.

name: Pulmonaria officinalis
tip: Spotted oval leaves and flowers that change from pink to blue-violet. Garden escape in woods and hedges, flowering early in spring.

name: Symphytum grandiflorum
tip: Low spreading comfrey with pale yellow-cream tubular flowers and hairy stems. Garden escape forming dense carpets under shade in woods and shady verges.

name: Symphytum officinale
tip: Tall hairy perennial with decurrent leaf bases forming wings on the stem and drooping bell-shaped clusters of cream, pink or purple flowers. Riverbanks, ditches and damp ground.

name: Symphytum orientale
tip: Grey-green softly hairy comfrey with white flowers, and stalked upper leaves unlike Common Comfrey. Naturalised garden escape on roadsides and waste ground, flowering early.

name: Symphytum tuberosum
tip: Slender comfrey with creamy-yellow flowers and unwinged stems, with a knobbly rhizome. Woodland and shady streamsides.

name: Alisma plantago-aquatica
tip: Tall hairless pond-edge plant with oval basal leaves and large branched pyramidal clusters of small three-petalled pale pink-white flowers. Ponds, canals and ditches.

name: Sagittaria sagittifolia
tip: Aquatic plant with distinctive arrow-shaped aerial leaves, ribbon-like submerged leaves and whorls of three-petalled white flowers with purple centres. Slow rivers and canals.

name: Aegopodium podagraria
tip: Spreading patch-forming plant of shady gardens and waste ground with leaves in threes of three toothed leaflets; flat white umbels, no bristles on fruit, lacks the tall stature of hogweed.

name: Aethusa cynapium
tip: Weed of cultivated ground with glossy, dark, finely cut leaves; the key clue is the long thread-like bracteoles hanging down beneath each small umbel, unlike Cow Parsley.

name: Angelica sylvestris
tip: Tall plant of damp meadows and woods with purplish stems and rounded, pinkish-tinged umbels; leaf stalks sheath the stem with inflated bases, unlike Hogweed.

name: Anthriscus caucalis
tip: Small annual of hedge banks and waste ground with tiny umbels of few rays and spiny-bristled fruits; flowers earlier and is smaller than Upright Hedge-parsley.

name: Anthriscus sylvestris
tip: Early-flowering roadside and hedgerow umbellifer with fine fern-like leaves and smooth, ridged, hollow stems; flowers April to June, well before Hogweed or Hemlock.

name: Berula erecta
tip: Wet-ground plant of ditches and stream margins with once-pinnate glossy leaves of many toothed leaflets, and leaf-like bracts under the umbels; hairless and creeping at base.

name: Chaerophyllum temulum
tip: Hairy hedgerow plant with purple-spotted, bristly swollen-jointed stems; flowers later than Cow Parsley and is much coarser to the touch with rough leaves.

name: Conium maculatum
tip: Tall, hairless, poisonous umbellifer with smooth stems blotched with purple and a mousy smell when crushed; much more finely cut and spotted than Cow Parsley or Angelica.

name: Conopodium majus
tip: Slender plant of old grassland and woodland edges whose feathery leaves are thread-like; stem leaves appear early, and a round edible tuber lies underground.

name: Daucus carota
tip: Umbels with divided, three-pronged bracts below and often a single dark red central floret; bird's-nest shape in fruit; found on chalk and coastal grassland.

name: Foeniculum vulgare
tip: Tall aniseed-scented plant with feathery thread-like leaves and flat yellow umbels, lacking bracts; found on coasts, waste ground and roadsides, unlike any other yellow umbellifer.

name: Heracleum mantegazzianum
tip: Huge plant to over 3 m with purple-blotched, thick bristly stems and giant umbels and leaves; sap can cause severe blistering, so do not touch. Far larger than Hogweed.

name: Heracleum sphondylium
tip: Common coarse umbellifer of verges and rough grass with hairy ridged stems and broad lobed leaves; much smaller than Giant Hogweed and often pinkish-white with unequal outer petals.

name: Myrrhis odorata
tip: Aniseed-scented, softly hairy plant of northern grassy verges with fern-like leaves often marked with white blotches; fruits are large, long and glossy brown.

name: Oenanthe crocata
tip: Very poisonous plant of ditches and wet places with celery-like glossy leaves, thick hollow stems and rounded umbels; sap turns yellowish-orange when cut.

name: Pastinaca sativa
tip: Only common umbellifer with yellow flowers and simple once-pinnate leaves with broad lobed leaflets; furrowed hairy stems, smelling of parsnip, on calcareous grassland.

name: Pimpinella major
tip: Taller than Burnet-saxifrage with a hollow, angled stem and undivided, deeply toothed leaflets on upper leaves; flowers white or pinkish, in hedgerows and damp grass.

name: Pimpinella saxifraga
tip: Slender, wiry plant of dry grassland with round-toothed lower leaflets and finely cut upper leaves; stem is solid, finely ridged and not angled, with no bracts.

name: Sanicula europaea
tip: Not a typical umbellifer: shiny, palmately lobed dark leaves and small rounded heads of tiny whitish or pinkish flowers in beech and oak woodland on lime-rich soil.

name: Silaum silaus
tip: Slender plant of old meadows on heavy soil with greenish-yellow flowers and finely cut, shiny leaves; stem ridged and slightly flushed purple, unlike pale-flowered umbellifers.

name: Sison amomum
tip: Slender, strong-smelling plant with a petrol-like odour and few-rayed small umbels of long unequal stalks; found on roadsides and hedgerows in southern England.

name: Smyrnium olusatrum
tip: Early-flowering coastal and roadside plant with glossy, bright green three-parted leaves and yellow-green flowers; black fruits and celery smell separate it from other umbellifers.

name: Torilis japonica
tip: Hairy, rough hedge-bank plant with small, white to pinkish umbels on long stalks and spiny fruits; flowers later than Cow Parsley, July onward, and has long stalks.

name: Torilis nodosa
tip: Low, spreading, often sprawling annual with tiny stalkless clusters of flowers opposite the leaves, and spiny knobbly fruit clusters; open dry grassland and field edges.

name: Erodium cicutarium
tip: Pink flowers with five petals and feathery pinnate leaves; fruit forms a long stork's bill; found on dry sandy and coastal soils, unlike the lobed leaves of Geranium.

name: Geranium columbinum
tip: Deep pink flowers on very long stalks; leaves are cut almost to the base into narrow lobes; fruits smooth. Found on dry calcareous grass and rocky slopes.

name: Geranium dissectum
tip: Small pink flowers with notched petals in pairs on short stalks; deeply cut leaves; sepals have a short point; fruits are hairy but beakless. Common on arable land.

name: Geranium endressii
tip: Garden escape with fairly large pink flowers veined darker, with a distinct white eye, and glossy deeply cut leaves; roadside and waste ground, mostly in the south-west.

name: Geranium lucidum
tip: Glossy, rounded, shallowly lobed leaves often tinged red, and small pink flowers with a wrinkled, keeled calyx; grows on walls, rocks and shady banks, especially on limestone.

name: Geranium macrorrhizum
tip: Garden escape with strongly aromatic, sticky hairy leaves, rounded shallow lobes and magenta-pink flowers with long protruding stamens; naturalised on banks and walls.

name: Geranium molle
tip: Soft, rounded, shallowly lobed grey-green leaves and pink flowers with deeply notched petals; fruits are smooth and wrinkled; common on lawns, verges and dry grassland.

name: Geranium pratense
tip: Large violet-blue flowers with dark veins in lush meadows and verges; deeply cut leaves; the largest-flowered wild blue crane's-bill, flowers more open than Wood Crane's-bill.

name: Geranium pusillum
tip: Tiny pale lilac to pinkish flowers with notched petals, and only five fertile stamens; leaves rounded with shallow lobes; soft hairy on disturbed bare ground.

name: Geranium pyrenaicum
tip: Mauve-purple flowers in pairs with deeply notched petals, larger than Dove's-foot, and softer leaves; stems have long soft hairs; grows on grassy verges and hedge banks.

name: Geranium robertianum
tip: Strongly smelling, often red-tinged plant with pinnately divided ferny leaves and small pink flowers with white stripes; shady walls, woods and shingle.

name: Geranium rotundifolium
tip: Softly hairy plant with round, shallowly lobed leaves and small pink flowers with unnotched petals; sepals have a short point; fruit smooth. Southern hedgebanks and walls.

name: Geranium sanguineum
tip: Large, bright magenta flowers with notched petals and deeply cut small leaves turning red in autumn; sprawling, on limestone grassland, sand dunes and coastal cliffs.

name: Geranium sylvaticum
tip: Violet-blue flowers with a whitish centre, more bowl-shaped than Meadow Crane's-bill; tall plant of northern upland meadows, woods and verges with deeply cut leaves.

name: Fallopia convolvulus
tip: Twining annual with small greenish flowers and heart-shaped leaves, lacking the large trumpet blooms of true bindweeds; arable fields and gardens, with dark, three-angled fruits.

name: Persicaria amphibia
tip: Pink flower spikes are broad and blunt; either floating glossy leaves in ponds and ditches or a hairy land form on damp soil.

name: Persicaria hydropiper
tip: Slender spikes of small greenish-pink flowers, drooping at the tips and speckled with glands; leaves have a hot peppery taste and wet places are favoured.

name: Persicaria lapathifolia
tip: Thick, dense, blunt spikes of pale pink to greenish-white flowers, usually nodding; stalks bear glands beneath; leaves often have a dark blotch. Arable fields and damp places.

name: Persicaria maculosa
tip: Spikes of pink flowers held upright, with stalks lacking glands, and leaves often with a dark blotch; reddish stem joints; common annual in arable land and waste ground.

name: Polygonum aviculare
tip: Mat-forming, wiry, much-branched annual with tiny flowers in leaf axils, tiny pink-edged green petals, and grey-green small leaves; trampled paths, arable fields and waste ground.

name: Rumex acetosa
tip: Sour-tasting dock with arrow-shaped leaves clasping the stem, and red-flushed flower spikes on separate male and female plants; common in meadows and grassland.

name: Rumex acetosella
tip: Small, slender sorrel with narrow spear-shaped leaves having outward-pointing basal lobes; reddish flower spikes, abundant on acid, sandy and heathy soils.

name: Rumex conglomeratus
tip: Branches are zigzag, spreading widely with flowers in distinct whorled clusters, each leafy; all three fruit valves bear a swollen wart; damp places.

name: Rumex crispus
tip: Narrow leaves with strongly crinkled, wavy margins; dense branched spikes, fruit valves with at most one wart; common on waste ground, shingle and arable land.

name: Rumex hydrolapathum
tip: Very tall dock of watersides with huge, long, lance-shaped leaves, and fruit valves all bearing warts; dense erect spikes, flowering later than most docks.

name: Rumex longifolius
tip: Large dock of northern streamsides and verges with broad leaves whose base is blunt or heart-shaped, and warts missing on the fruit valves; mostly upland and northern.

name: Rumex obtusifolius
tip: Familiar weed with broad, heart-based leaves and fruit valves with toothed margins and a single wart; spikes less crowded than Curled Dock; also fields and gardens.

name: Rumex sanguineus
tip: Slender dock with erect, spreading branches, narrow leaves and fruit with a single wart; leaf veins may be red in var. sanguineus; shady woods and hedgerows.

name: Juncus acutiflorus
tip: Tall tufted rush of wet pastures with dark, pointed flower heads and hollow cross-partitioned leaves; branches of the inflorescence spread out; tepals are pointed.

name: Juncus articulatus
tip: Rush of wet ground with flattened or knotty stems and leaves with visible cross-partitions; flowers dark in clusters whose tepals are pointed; fruits glossy and blunt, shorter than similar rushes.

name: Juncus bufonius
tip: Small spreading annual of wet bare paths and pond edges with slender branched stems and flowers singly along the branches, green tepals with a white edge.

name: Juncus bulbosus
tip: Weak, slender, often floating rush of acid bogs and pools whose base swells into bulb-like tufts; flowers are tiny, green and clustered in small heads.

name: Juncus conglomeratus
tip: Green, soft tufted rush with finely ridged stems and an inflorescence appearing from the side, held tight in compact flower clusters; pith is interrupted and stem ridged when dry.

name: Juncus effusus
tip: Common tufted rush of damp pastures with smooth, glossy, unribbed green stems when fresh and continuous white pith; flower cluster arises low on stem, often loose.

name: Juncus gerardii
tip: Fine, flat leaves with bristly dark flower heads in saltmarshes; two-ranked leaves and brownish-black tepals; grows in salt-influenced grassland near the coast.

name: Juncus inflexus
tip: Blue-green, strongly ridged stiff stems with interrupted pith, and flower clusters emerging well below the stem tip; found in wet, heavy clay or calcareous soils.

name: Juncus squarrosus
tip: Tufted rush with a rosette of stiff, grooved, curved leaves and dark flower spikes; typical of acid moorland, bog and heath, quite unlike other rushes.

name: Juncus tenuis
tip: Wiry, slender rush of paths and tracks with long leafy bracts overtopping the loose cluster of pale green-brown flowers; naturalised in North American origin.

name: Luzula campestris
tip: Short, early-flowering grass-like plant with hairy leaves and spread-out clusters of dark brown flowers with yellow anthers; lawns and meadows; flowers earlier than other wood-rushes.

name: Luzula multiflora
tip: Clump-forming and hairy-leaved, with flowers in several dense brown heads on stalks of unequal length; acid grassland and heaths, flowering later than Field Wood-rush.

name: Luzula pilosa
tip: Woodland species with broad, hairy grass-like leaves and flowers solitary on drooping stalks, then fruits that bend down; the flowers are chestnut brown.

name: Luzula sylvatica
tip: Large tussock-forming wood-rush with glossy, broad, shiny leaves edged with long hairs; dense brown flower heads in spring; grows in damp, shady woods and on mountain ledges.

name: Centranthus ruber
tip: Pink-red, occasionally white, flowers in dense clusters, each with a short spur; grey-green fleshy leaves; naturalised on old walls, cliffs and railway lines.

name: Dipsacus fullonum
tip: Very tall prickly biennial with egg-shaped spiny heads and long curved bracts, flowering as a purple ring; basal leaves form water-holding cups; rough grassland and verges.

name: Knautia arvensis
tip: Rounded heads of lilac-blue flowers, outer florets larger, on tall stems; lobed leaves; tall and hairy, unlike Small Scabious; found on dry grassland and verges.

name: Leycesteria formosa
tip: Shrub with hollow green bamboo-like stems and hanging spikes of white flowers among purple-red bracts, followed by dark berries; garden escape on waste ground.

name: Lonicera japonica
tip: Twining semi-evergreen climber with paired, fragrant white flowers ageing yellow, and black berries; rare escape, differing from native Honeysuckle in having hairy shoots.

name: Lonicera periclymenum
tip: Native twining climber of hedges and woods with pairs of tubular, creamy yellow flowers flushed pink, strongly scented at night; red berries in clusters in autumn.

name: Scabiosa columbaria
tip: Slender plant of dry chalk and limestone grassland with blue-lilac flower heads, and finely cut leaves on stems; shorter and less hairy than Field Scabious.

name: Succisa pratensis
tip: Rounded dark blue-purple heads on a plant with undivided oval, untoothed leaves in damp grassland, bog and heath; blooms later than the other scabious species.

name: Symphoricarpos albus
tip: Suckering shrub with oval opposite leaves and small pinkish bell flowers followed by large white spongy berries; escape from gardens, hedges and waste ground.

name: Valeriana dioica
tip: Small, dioecious plant of wet meadows and fens with undivided basal leaves and pinnate stem leaves; clusters of tiny pale pink flowers, spreading by runners.

name: Valeriana officinalis
tip: Tall plant with pinnate leaves of many toothed leaflets and dense clusters of pale pink flowers; stout, hairy and grooved stem, and a distinctive smell; damp places.

name: Valerianella carinata
tip: Small annual of arable fields and bare ground with tiny pale flowers in forked clusters; fruit is keeled, with a groove, which distinguishes it from Common Cornsalad.

name: Valerianella locusta
tip: Low forking annual with tiny pale blue flowers in clusters and spoon-shaped leaves; fruit flattened with a corky swelling on one side; dry banks, walls and arable.

name: Blackstonia perfoliata
tip: Blue-grey plant of chalk and limestone grassland with paired leaves fused around the stem and bright yellow flowers having eight petals that close in dull weather.

name: Centaurium erythraea
tip: Pink flowers with five petals and a yellow centre, in flat-topped clusters; stem leaves are oval, with a basal rosette; dry grassland, dunes and woodland rides.

name: Gentianella amarella
tip: Purple flowers with five petals and a fringe of hairs in the throat, with a tube typically five-lobed; chalk grassland and dunes, flowering late; Field Gentian is four-lobed.

name: Circaea lutetiana
tip: Shade-loving woodland and garden weed with paired opposite oval leaves and slender spikes of tiny white flowers with only two notched petals; fruits are bristly burs.

name: Epilobium brunnescens
tip: Tiny mat-forming willowherb with creeping rooting stems, rounded little leaves and solitary small flowers; common on paths, walls and rocky ground, mostly in the north and west.

name: Epilobium ciliatum
tip: Upright, often branching willowherb with narrow leaves, small pale pink flowers and glandular hairs on the upper stem; the seed pods are glandular too. Common weed of gardens and waste ground.

name: Epilobium hirsutum
tip: Tall, stout, softly hairy willowherb of ditches and streamsides with large rose-pink flowers and a four-lobed stigma; leaves clasp the stem and smell faintly fruity.

name: Epilobium montanum
tip: Common willowherb of shady places and walls with short-stalked or unstalked, broad, opposite oval leaves, small pink flowers with a four-lobed stigma and a rounded, hairy stem.

name: Epilobium obscurum
tip: Slender willowherb of damp ground with a stem bearing raised lines, small pink flowers and short pods; leaves are narrow, stalkless and often reddish. Spreads by leafy runners in autumn.

name: Epilobium palustre
tip: Slender willowherb of bogs and fens with narrow, nearly untoothed leaves, small pale pink or whitish flowers and a rounded stem covered in short curved hairs.

name: Epilobium parviflorum
tip: Softly shaggy willowherb of wet places with stalkless, soft-hairy leaves and larger pink flowers than other small ones, with a four-lobed stigma; stem has spreading hairs.

name: Epilobium roseum
tip: Slender willowherb with distinct leaf stalks, tiny white flowers fading pink, and a club-shaped, unlobed stigma; grows in gardens, shade and waste places.

name: Epilobium tetragonum
tip: Upright willowherb with a stem bearing four raised lines, narrow stalkless leaves and small pink flowers with a four-lobed stigma; lacks glandular hairs. Common on open, disturbed ground.

name: Fuchsia magellanica
tip: Garden escape shrub, widely used in hedges in the west, with dangling flowers with red tubes and sepals and purple petals; leaves are oval, in whorls or pairs.

name: Oenothera biennis
tip: Tall biennial of sands and waste ground with pale yellow flowers opening at dusk; flowers are smaller than Large-flowered Evening-primrose and sepals are green without red stripes.

name: Oenothera glazioviana
tip: Tall, robust evening-primrose of dunes and waste ground with big bright yellow flowers, red-based hairs on the stem and red-striped buds, flowers larger than Common Evening-primrose.

name: Anacamptis pyramidalis
tip: Orchid of chalk and limestone grassland with a dense, conical, bright pink flower head that turns dome-like; long spur on each flower and unspotted narrow leaves.

name: Dactylorhiza fuchsii
tip: Commonest British orchid of grassland and verges; pale pink to white flowers with looped, dashed lines on a three-lobed lip and spotted leaves; spike is cone-shaped.

name: Dactylorhiza incarnata
tip: Orchid of damp fens and meadows with narrow, upright, unspotted leaves hooded at the tip and flowers whose lip edges fold back; flowers vary in colour from flesh to purple.

name: Dactylorhiza maculata
tip: Small, slender spotted-orchid of acid heath and bog with pale pink flowers, a rounded shallow-lobed lip with the middle lobe tiny, and short spotted leaves.

name: Dactylorhiza praetermissa
tip: Stout marsh-orchid of damp lowland meadows, dunes and fens with unspotted or lightly spotted broad leaves and a dense head of deep magenta flowers with a broad lip.

name: Dactylorhiza purpurella
tip: Marsh-orchid of northern wet meadows, deep purple flowers with a diamond-shaped lip and dark flower stalks and bracts; leaves are unspotted or ringed with spots, shorter than Southern.

name: Epipactis helleborine
tip: Tall woodland orchid with oval, ribbed, spirally arranged leaves and a one-sided spike of nodding dull green and purple-pink flowers; often grows in shade, in hedgerows and urban spots.

name: Neottia cordata
tip: Tiny orchid of moorland among heather and moss, with one pair of small heart-shaped leaves and a few minute reddish-green flowers; much smaller than Common Twayblade.

name: Neottia ovata
tip: Orchid of woods, meadows and dunes with just two large oval opposite leaves at mid-stem and a long spike of yellow-green flowers with a forked lip.

name: Ophrys apifera
tip: Orchid of calcareous grass and quarries with flowers resembling a bumblebee, pink petals and a brown velvety lip with yellow markings; stems bear a few narrow leaves.

name: Orchis mascula
tip: Spring orchid of woods and meadows with leaves usually blotched purple-black, a loose spike of magenta flowers and a long spur; smells unpleasantly of tomcat in older flowers.

name: Platanthera chlorantha
tip: Orchid of woods and meadows with two large oval leaves near base and greenish-white flowers with parallel pollen sacks; flowers are larger than Lesser Butterfly-orchid and scented at night.

name: Asplenium adiantum-nigrum
tip: Evergreen fern of walls, rocks and hedge banks with glossy dark triangular, twice-cut fronds on a shiny blackish stalk; lacks the green stalk of other spleenworts.

name: Asplenium ceterach
tip: Small fern of limestone walls and rocks with leathery lobed fronds densely covered beneath with overlapping rusty brown scales; may shrivel in drought and revive after rain.

name: Asplenium ruta-muraria
