tip: Tiny tufted fern of limestone walls and mortar with dark green, stiff, wedge-shaped, toothed leaflets on a short stalk; leaflets resemble those of rue.

name: Asplenium scolopendrium
tip: Fern with undivided, glossy, strap-shaped fronds with wavy edge and rows of brown spore lines underneath; common in shady lanes, walls and wood banks.

name: Asplenium trichomanes
tip: Small evergreen fern of walls and rocks with narrow once-cut fronds, tiny oval leaflets along a glossy black stalk; leaflets are regular and green.

name: Athyrium filix-femina
tip: Large, delicate, lime-green fern of damp woods, with twice-cut fronds forming a shuttlecock; the spore patches are curved or hooked and the stalk base is scaly.

name: Blechnum spicant
tip: Fern of acid woods and heaths with two types of frond: sterile ones are glossy, once-cut and in a flat rosette, while fertile ones are upright and narrow.

name: Cystopteris fragilis
tip: Small delicate fern of walls, rock crevices and mountains with thin twice-cut fronds and round spore patches under a hood; fronds die back in winter.

name: Gymnocarpium dryopteris
tip: Delicate creeping fern of shady rocky woods and screes with a pale, triangular frond divided into three roughly equal branches; fronds are held flat.

name: Oreopteris limbosperma
tip: Tufted fern of hill slopes and acid woods with fronds tapering at both ends and smelling of lemon when crushed; the lowest pinnae are tiny. Has yellow glands beneath.

name: Phegopteris connectilis
tip: Fern of damp, shady rocky banks with a triangular, pale green hairy frond with the lowest pair of leaflets bent down and pointing forwards; fronds are held flat.

name: Populus alba
tip: Large suckering tree with leaves that are lobed and maple-like and snowy-white felted beneath; bark is pale with diamond-shaped marks. Catkins appear early spring.

name: Populus nigra
tip: Rare native tree of floodplains with big burry trunk, drooping branches and triangular, finely toothed hairless leaves; female trees are scarce. Hybrid poplars are far more frequent.

name: Populus tremula
tip: Poplar with rounded leaves on long flat stalks, so they tremble in even a slight breeze; forms suckering thickets on heaths, woodland edges and in the north.

name: Salix alba
tip: Large riverside willow with narrow, silky silvery-hairy leaves on both sides; catkins appear with the leaves, and branches are upright and yellow-green.

name: Salix aurita
tip: Small shrubby willow of damp heath and woods with wrinkled, grey-hairy oval leaves with a twisted tip and ear-like leafy stipules at the base of the leaf stalk.

name: Salix caprea
tip: Large shrub or small tree with broad oval, wavy leaves, grey-felted beneath, and large fat silky catkins (pussy willow) before the leaves in early spring.

name: Salix cinerea
tip: Common bushy willow of wet ground with oval leaves grey-hairy beneath and short hairy twigs; rusty-haired in one subspecies, with ridges under the bark when stripped.

name: Salix pentandra
tip: Shrubby willow of northern damp ground with glossy dark green, bay-like, leathery leaves that are aromatic when crushed; catkins appear late, after the leaves.

name: Salix purpurea
tip: Slender shrub of wet places with narrow bluish-green leaves that are often paired or opposite and bitter; catkins are narrow, with purple anthers.

name: Salix repens
tip: Low straggly shrub of heaths, bogs and dunes with small oval grey-silky leaves underneath; catkins small and upright, stems often sprawling or creeping underground.

name: Salix viminalis
tip: Tall shrub often grown in osier beds, with very long narrow leaves white silky-felted beneath and long straight unbranched shoots.

name: Euphrasia arctica
tip: Small semi-parasitic eyebright of northern and western coasts and grassland with whitish to lilac flowers; best identified by habitat, glandular hairs and the leaf shape. Hard to separate from other eyebrights.

name: Euphrasia confusa
tip: Tufted eyebright of heath and acid grassland, with white or lilac flowers and toothed leaves; very similar to other eyebrights, which need careful examination to separate.

name: Euphrasia micrantha
tip: Small eyebright of heaths and dry grassland, with tiny pale lilac to whitish flowers, glandular hairs, and slender unbranched or sparsely branched stems.

name: Euphrasia nemorosa
tip: The commonest eyebright of grassland and heaths, with white or lilac flowers with a yellow spot and purple veins, and sharply toothed, dark-green leaves; no hairs on glands.

name: Melampyrum pratense
tip: Semi-parasitic annual of woods and heaths with opposite narrow leaves and pale yellow, closed tubular flowers in pairs, all facing one side of the stem.

name: Odontites vernus
tip: Branched annual of grassy and disturbed ground with narrow toothed leaves and spikes of small pink-red flowers, with a one-sided flowering spike; stems often reddish.

name: Orobanche minor
tip: Leafless, yellowish-brown parasitic plant with scales rather than leaves, usually on clovers and other legumes; flowers have a purple-tinged tube and curved lip.

name: Pedicularis palustris
tip: Hairless plant of wet meadows and fens with finely cut, fern-like leaves and clustered pink-red flowers with a toothed hood; stem often branched.

name: Pedicularis sylvatica
tip: Low plant of damp heaths and moors with finely cut leaves and pink flowers on short stems; calyx is inflated and stems are sprawling, unlike taller Marsh Lousewort.

name: Rhinanthus minor
tip: Semi-parasitic annual of meadows, with bright yellow flowers in a leafy spike, inflated seed pods that rattle when ripe, and narrow, coarsely toothed opposite leaves.

name: Ceratocapnos claviculata
tip: Delicate climber of acid woods and heaths using tendril-tipped leaves and clusters of tiny cream flowers; the leaves are divided into small oval leaflets.

name: Chelidonium majus
tip: Plant of hedge banks and walls, with brittle stems that bleed orange latex, blue-green deeply cut leaves and clusters of small four-petalled yellow flowers.

name: Eschscholzia californica
tip: Garden escape of verges and waste ground with bright orange-yellow, silky four-petalled flowers and blue-green finely divided leaves.

name: Fumaria muralis
tip: Scrambling fumitory of arable and waste ground, with relatively large pink flowers with dark red tips, and stalks that are short compared with Common Fumitory.

name: Fumaria officinalis
tip: Weedy fumitory with grey-green finely cut leaves and spikes of small pink flowers tipped with dark red-purple; sepals are small and narrower than the corolla.

name: Papaver dubium
tip: Poppy with paler scarlet flowers, hairs pressed against the stem, and a long narrow smooth seed capsule; the capsule is more than twice as long as it is wide.

name: Papaver rhoeas
tip: Familiar field poppy with bright scarlet petals, often with a dark blotch, spreading hairs on stems and a rounded, smooth seed capsule.

name: Papaver somniferum
tip: Tall blue-grey poppy of waste ground and gardens, hairless, with large white, pink or mauve flowers often dark at the base and big globe-like seed capsules.

name: Pseudofumaria lutea
tip: Tufted garden escape on old walls and rocks with soft, fern-like blue-green leaves and many tubular yellow flowers; long flowering season.

name: Cruciata laevipes
tip: Hairy bedstraw of grassland and hedge banks with whorls of four oval, three-veined leaves and tiny yellow honey-scented flower clusters in leaf axils.

name: Galium album
tip: Tall bedstraw of hedges and verges with whorls of narrow leaves, a square smooth stem and frothy clusters of white flowers; flowers larger than those of Lady's Bedstraw.

name: Galium aparine
tip: Sticky scrambler of hedges and gardens with whorls of narrow leaves, a rough stem and leaves covered in hooked hairs that cling to clothes; flowers tiny greenish-white.

name: Galium odoratum
tip: Low woodland plant of shady spots, with whorls of narrow-oval leaves and clusters of small white flowers, and a hay-like smell when dried.

name: Galium palustre
tip: Straggly bedstraw of wet meadows and ditches with whorls of blunt narrow leaves, black when dry, and loose clusters of white flowers; stem is square and smooth.

name: Galium saxatile
tip: Low, mat-forming bedstraw of acid grass and heaths, with small bristle-tipped leaves in whorls, backward-pointing, and dense clusters of white flowers.

name: Galium uliginosum
tip: Slender bedstraw of calcareous fens with leaves in whorls with prickles that point forwards and leaf tips with a bristle; stems are rough, with a loose white flower cluster.

name: Galium verum
tip: Bedstraw of dry grassland and dunes with frothy masses of tiny golden-yellow, honey-scented flowers and narrow whorled leaves with black edges that curl under.

name: Sherardia arvensis
tip: Small sprawling annual of arable ground and dry banks with whorls of narrow leaves and tiny pink to lilac flower heads, each surrounded by leafy bracts.

name: Arum italicum
tip: Arum with arrow-shaped leaves with pale veins appearing in autumn, and a yellow spadix; leaf lobes spread apart. Unlike native Lords-and-ladies, it is in leaf in winter.

name: Arum maculatum
tip: Woodland and hedgerow arum with arrow-shaped leaves, sometimes spotted purple, and a hooded green spathe round a purple or yellow spadix; spikes of orange-red berries in autumn.

name: Lemna gibba
tip: Floating duckweed whose rounded fronds are swollen and spongy-looking underneath; fronds are bigger and more rounded than Common Duckweed. Flowers are seldom seen.

name: Lemna minor
tip: The common duckweed of still ponds, with small flat oval single-rooted fronds, three-veined and floating; flowers are rare and very tiny.

name: Lemna minuta
tip: Tiny non-native duckweed with very small, narrow-oval fronds having one vein, and spreads rapidly on ponds; smaller than Common Duckweed. Flowers are very rare.

name: Lemna trisulca
tip: Duckweed submerged under the water surface, with translucent, flat, lance-shaped fronds joined in branching crosses, and only reaches surface during flowering.

name: Lysichiton americanus
tip: Large garden escape of wet woods and stream banks with huge, cabbage-like leaves, and a bright yellow hooded spathe appearing in spring; has a skunk-like smell.

name: Allium paradoxum
tip: Spring white drooping umbel with few flowers and bulbils among them; flat, broad, keeled leaves smelling of garlic; a garden escape on verges and hedgebanks, unlike Three-cornered Garlic.

name: Allium triquetrum
tip: Sharply three-angled flower stem and drooping one-sided cluster of white bells with green stripes; a garden escape on banks and verges, mostly in the south and west.

name: Allium ursinum
tip: Carpets damp woods with strong garlic smell; broad oval stalked leaves and a rounded umbel of star-like white flowers distinguish it from other wild garlics.

name: Allium vineale
tip: Slender hollow cylindrical leaves and a pinkish-green head often with bulbils and long-beaked spathe; grassy places and verges in summer, unlike the white-flowered garlics.

name: Galanthus nivalis
tip: Early nodding white flower with three long outer petals and a green-marked inner ring; grey-green flat leaves; woods and churchyards in late winter.

name: Leucojum aestivum
tip: Taller than Snowdrop with several white bells, each petal tipped green, on one stem; wet meadows and riverbanks in spring, mainly Thames valley and Ireland.

name: Narcissus poeticus
tip: Flat white petals around a small yellow cup edged red, fragrant, one flower per stem; late-flowering, in grassland or as an escape.

name: Narcissus pseudonarcissus
tip: Smaller than garden daffodils with pale yellow twisted petals and a deeper yellow trumpet; grassy woods and meadows in early spring.

name: Calluna vulgaris
tip: Tiny scale-like leaves pressed along the stem and small pale pink-purple bells with a prominent calyx; common on moors and heaths, later than the other heaths.

name: Empetrum nigrum
tip: Low evergreen with needle-like leaves grooved beneath, tiny pinkish flowers in leaf axils and black berries; moorland and mountain heath, unlike heathers.

name: Erica cinerea
tip: Bright reddish-purple bells in whorled clusters along the shoots; dry heaths and rocky slopes, flowering earlier than Cross-leaved Heath, which is paler and on wet ground.

name: Erica tetralix
tip: Pale pink bells in a terminal head and grey downy leaves in whorls of four forming a cross; wet heaths and bogs.

name: Rhododendron ponticum
tip: Large evergreen shrub with big glossy leaves and mauve-purple trumpet flowers in domed clusters; invasive in woods and heaths, dense and shading everything below.

name: Vaccinium myrtillus
tip: Small green angular twigs, bright green deciduous toothed leaves and solitary globular pinkish-green flowers; acid woods and moors with blue-black berries.

name: Vaccinium oxycoccos
tip: Wiry creeping stems with tiny oval leaves white underneath and pink flowers with swept-back petals; wet bogs and sphagnum lawns.

name: Vaccinium vitis-idaea
tip: Evergreen leathery leaves dotted beneath with black glands and a nodding cluster of white-pink bells; upland moors and pinewoods, red berries.

name: Campanula latifolia
tip: Tall leafy plant with large blue-purple bells in a leafy spike; stem rounded and hairy, leaves coarse and pointed; shady woods, north England and Scotland.

name: Campanula persicifolia
tip: Wide open bowl-shaped blue flowers on a slender stem with narrow, shiny, finely toothed leaves; a garden escape on banks and verges.

name: Campanula portenschlagiana
tip: Mat-forming wall plant with dense violet star-shaped bells, deeply five-lobed, and small rounded toothed leaves; garden escape on walls and pavements.

name: Campanula poscharskyana
tip: Sprawling plant with pale lilac starry flowers cut nearly to the base and heart-shaped toothed leaves; naturalised on walls and banks.

name: Campanula rotundifolia
tip: Slender nodding pale blue bells on wiry stems; basal leaves rounded, stem leaves very narrow; grassland and dunes, late summer.

name: Campanula trachelium
tip: Tall, roughly hairy, angular stem with nettle-like coarse toothed leaves and large blue-purple bells; woods and hedgerows, mainly lowland England and Wales.

name: Jasione montana
tip: Looks like a scabious but with a rounded blue pom-pom head of fused-based petals and no bracts like a daisy; dry acid grass and cliffs.

name: Lobelia erinus
tip: Small blue bedding plant with two-lipped flowers with a white eye, straggling stems and toothed leaves; occasional escape on pavements and walls.

name: Cyclamen hederifolium
tip: Pink swept-back petals appearing before marbled, angular ivy-like leaves; naturalised in woods and churchyards in autumn.

name: Lysimachia nemorum
tip: Creeping woodland plant with solitary star-like yellow flowers on slender stalks and pointed oval paired leaves; shady woods and streamsides.

name: Lysimachia nummularia
tip: Trailing mat with rounded paired leaves and large cup-shaped yellow flowers singly in leaf axils; damp grass and riverbanks.

name: Lysimachia punctata
tip: Garden escape with whorled hairy leaves and whorls of yellow flowers with fringed edges and orange spots; stands upright on verges and waste ground.

name: Lysimachia vulgaris
tip: Tall plant of waterside with paired or whorled lance-shaped leaves and big branched panicle of yellow flowers; riverbanks and fens.

name: Primula veris
tip: Nodding one-sided cluster of small deep yellow, scented flowers with tubular calyx on a tall stem from a rosette of wrinkled leaves; grassland, April.

name: Primula vulgaris
tip: Pale yellow solitary flowers on separate hairy stalks from a rosette of crinkled leaves; woods, banks and hedges in early spring.

name: Samolus valerandi
tip: Small white flowers in a loose spike with a ring of tiny scales within; spoon-shaped leaves; damp coastal places and flushes, unlike the primulas.

name: Dryopteris affinis
tip: Golden-brown scaly stalk and glossy leathery fronds with blunt, toothed tips of pinnules near the tip; darker spot at pinnule bases; woods and hedgebanks.

name: Dryopteris carthusiana
tip: Pale green, triangular, finely divided fronds held at an angle, with pale scales on stalk; damp woods and fens, rarer than Broad Buckler-fern.

name: Dryopteris dilatata
tip: Large spreading arching fronds with darker central blotch on scales and dark-centred stalk scales; widespread in woods, the commonest buckler-fern.

name: Dryopteris filix-mas
tip: Shuttlecock of tall dull green fronds with rounded pinnule tips and a dark spot where pinnules join the midrib; common in woods and hedgerows.

name: Polypodium interjectum
tip: Evergreen fern on walls, trees and rocks with fronds longest in the middle; sori oval and fronds with finely toothed tips, unlike the other polypody.

name: Polypodium vulgare
tip: Evergreen rock and tree fern with once-cut fronds having parallel sides and blunt tips; round orange sori; differs from Intermediate Polypody by rounded outline.

name: Polystichum aculeatum
tip: Stiff, glossy dark green fronds with spiny, bristle-tipped pinnules that overlap and are once divided; woods and shaded banks.

name: Polystichum setiferum
tip: Soft, drooping, twice-cut fronds with bristle-tipped pinnules, thinner than Hard Shield-fern; shaded lanes and woods in the west.

name: Hypericum androsaemum
tip: Shrubby plant with large paired oval leaves, yellow flowers in small clusters and berry-like fruit that turns from red to black; woods and hedgerows.

name: Hypericum calycinum
tip: Evergreen garden shrub with big solitary yellow flowers full of stamens; spreads by suckers on banks and waste ground.

name: Hypericum hirsutum
tip: Softly hairy stem and leaves without translucent dots on leaf edges; woods and hedges, with pale yellow flowers and black-dotted sepals.

name: Hypericum humifusum
tip: Low sprawling wiry plant with small pale yellow flowers and small leaves with black dots; acid heaths and tracks, shorter than other St John's-worts.

name: Hypericum maculatum
tip: Stem with four raised lines and few or no translucent dots on leaves; sepals blunt and not pointed; grassland, scrub and woods.

name: Hypericum perforatum
tip: Stem with two raised lines and leaves full of see-through dots when held to the light; common on grassland, verges and scrub.

name: Hypericum pulchrum
tip: Slender plant with round stem and red-tinged buds, flowers with red streaks beneath; leaves clasping with transparent dots; heaths and acid grass.

name: Hypericum tetrapterum
tip: Stem with four narrow wings on the angles and translucent dots on the leaves; wet meadows, ditches and fens.

name: Larix decidua
tip: Deciduous conifer with soft needles in tufts, bright green in spring; cones small with straight scales and twigs yellowish, unlike Japanese Larch.

name: Larix kaempferi
tip: Deciduous conifer with blue-green needles, reddish twigs and cones with scales curved back like a rose; widely planted, unlike European Larch.

name: Picea abies
tip: Typical Christmas-tree spruce with hanging long cones and four-sided needles that are not sharp; planted widely in forests.

name: Picea sitchensis
tip: Spruce with sharp, spiky flattened needles, blue-white beneath, and short cones with papery scales; widely planted in wet upland forests.

name: Pinus contorta
tip: Pine with paired twisted dark green needles and small prickly cones that stay on the tree; planted on poor wet peaty ground.

name: Pinus nigra
tip: Tall pine with long, grey-green, twisted needles in pairs and a straight trunk; planted on sandy soils and coasts, unlike Scots Pine.

name: Pinus sylvestris
tip: Pine with short blue-green paired needles, orange-red upper bark and flat-topped crown with age; native pinewoods and widely planted.

name: Tsuga heterophylla
tip: Conifer with drooping leading shoot, short flat needles of unequal lengths with white lines beneath, and tiny cones; shady forestry plantations.

name: Viola arvensis
tip: Small cream-yellow flowers shorter than the sepals, with a little purple at times; arable fields and disturbed ground, unlike larger Wild Pansy.

name: Viola canina
tip: Blue flowers with pale spur, narrow oval leaves and no basal rosette; heaths and dry grassland, slender and often less leafy than other dog-violets.

name: Viola hirta
tip: Scentless violet with distinctly hairy stalks and leaves, narrow leaf base lobes and pale violet flowers; calcareous grassland and scrub.

name: Viola odorata
tip: Fragrant violet with runners, deep violet or white flowers and rounded heart-shaped leaves; hedgebanks and woodland edges, early spring.

name: Viola palustris
tip: Pale lilac flowers with darker veins, kidney-shaped hairless leaves and creeping stems; wet bogs and marshes.

name: Viola reichenbachiana
tip: Violet with dark, narrow, straight spur and narrow petals that do not overlap; no leaf rosette in flower; woods and hedgebanks.

name: Viola riviniana
tip: Common violet with pale, thick, notched spur and overlapping bluer petals; rosette of heart-shaped leaves; woods, hedges and grassland.

name: Viola tricolor
tip: Large flowers of purple, yellow or mixed colour, petals longer than sepals; deeply lobed leafy stipules; grassland and dunes.

name: Atriplex glabriuscula
tip: Fleshy prostrate coastal orache with triangular leaves, spreading and mealy; found on shingle and strandlines, with fruiting bracts joined at base.

name: Atriplex littoralis
tip: Narrow, linear toothed leaves; upright, mainly in saltmarsh and coastal edges, differs from other oraches in narrow leaves.

name: Atriplex patula
tip: Arable weed with leaves narrowly triangular with basal lobes and fruiting bracts stalkless, toothed; stem stripes green and red; waste land.

name: Atriplex prostrata
tip: Leaves triangular with spreading basal lobes, silvery-mealy when young, often on saltmarshes and disturbed ground; fruiting bracts often stalked.

name: Beta vulgaris
tip: Glossy dark green fleshy leaves, coastal; tall flower spikes with green flowers, shingle and sea walls, wild ancestor of beetroot.

name: Chenopodium album
tip: Common weed with mealy white-dusted leaves, diamond-shaped to toothed, and dense green flower clusters; arable and waste ground.

name: Chenopodium ficifolium
tip: Leaves with three lobes, central lobe long, parallel-sided, near-hairless; arable and disturbed ground, unlike Fat-hen.

name: Castanea sativa
tip: Large tree with long toothed glossy leaves, long yellowish catkins and spiny husked nuts; deeply spiralled bark in older trees.

name: Fagus sylvatica
tip: Smooth grey bark, silky hairy edges to young glossy wavy-edged leaves and tiny catkins; tall woodland tree with copper autumn colour.

name: Quercus cerris
tip: Oak with bristly acorn cups and narrow pointed lobed leaves, rough on the surface; planted tree in parks, spreading in the south.

name: Quercus ilex
tip: Evergreen oak with dark leathery leaves white-felted beneath, often spiny when young; widely planted and naturalised near coasts.

name: Quercus petraea
tip: Oak with long-stalked leaves and stalkless acorns; leaf base wedge-shaped with star-hairs on veins beneath; mainly western upland woods.

name: Quercus robur
tip: Oak with stalked acorns on long stems and almost stalkless leaves with small ear-like lobes at base; common in lowland woods and hedges.

name: Quercus rubra
tip: Planted oak with large leaves having pointed bristle-tipped lobes, turning red in autumn; acorn cups flat and shallow.

name: Adoxa moschatellina
tip: Tiny green-yellow flowers clustered in a cube-shaped head of five, four facing sideways and one up; woodland, spring, smells musky.

name: Sambucus nigra
tip: Shrub or small tree with flat heads of creamy-white scented flowers and compound leaves; hedgerows and waste ground, black berries in autumn.

name: Viburnum lantana
tip: Shrub with leaves wrinkled and covered by greyish star-shaped down, flat white flower heads; chalk scrub and hedges, black berries.

name: Viburnum opulus
tip: Shrub with maple-like lobed leaves, flat flower heads with large sterile white flowers around the rim and red berries; damp woods and fens.

name: Euphorbia amygdaloides
tip: Shady woodland spurge with evergreen, dark, hairy leaves in rosettes and reddish stems; yellow-green bracts form a branched head in spring, unlike the annual field spurges.

name: Euphorbia exigua
tip: Small slender annual of arable fields and bare ground with very narrow, grass-like leaves tipped with a tiny point; bracts are narrow and crescent-shaped glands have two horns.

name: Euphorbia helioscopia
tip: Common annual of cultivated land with rounded, finely toothed leaves broadest near the tip and a flat-topped umbel of five rays, like a tiny sun.

name: Euphorbia lathyris
tip: Tall, blue-green biennial with crossed pairs of long narrow leaves up the stem; garden escape with fat green caper-like fruits.

name: Euphorbia peplus
tip: Small garden weed with smooth, stalked, blue-green oval leaves and a three-rayed umbel; glands bear long slender horns, unlike toothed Sun Spurge.

name: Mercurialis annua
tip: Weed of gardens and arable land with bright green, shiny toothed leaves; male and female flowers on separate plants, tiny and green, in leaf axils. Stem is branched and brittle.

name: Mercurialis perennis
tip: Carpeting woodland perennial of ancient woods, unbranched hairy stems with toothed dark green leaves; tiny green flowers in early spring, poisonous and unscented.

name: Potamogeton berchtoldii
tip: Slender submerged pondweed with narrow, translucent, three-veined leaves tapering to a point and flowers held in small short spikes; leaves are broader than in Lesser Pondweed.

name: Potamogeton crispus
tip: Submerged pondweed with distinctive wavy, finely toothed, crinkled translucent leaves like seaweed; stems flattened and reddish-brown, in ponds, canals and ditches.

name: Potamogeton natans
tip: Common pondweed with floating, leathery, oval leaves on long stalks with a distinct joint near the blade; also narrow submerged leaves; flower spike held above water.

name: Potamogeton perfoliatus
tip: Submerged pondweed whose broad, oval, translucent leaves clasp the stem at the base, with no stalks and no floating leaves; in clear, base-rich water.

name: Potamogeton polygonifolius
tip: Pondweed of acid pools, bog ditches and streams, with oval floating leaves on long stalks that lack the joint seen in Broad-leaved Pondweed; also lance-shaped submerged leaves.

name: Potamogeton pusillus
tip: Slender, fine submerged pondweed with narrow, linear, three-veined leaves with a blunt or short-pointed tip and no floating leaves; spikes of few widely spaced flowers.

name: Zannichellia palustris
tip: Thread-like submerged plant with opposite, very narrow grass-like leaves and tiny flowers in the leaf axils; the curved, beaked fruits in clusters distinguish it.

name: Alcea rosea
tip: Very tall garden plant self-seeding on walls and pavements, with large, funnel-shaped flowers in many colours on stout hairy spikes and big rounded, lobed leaves.

name: Malva moschata
tip: Roadside and grassland mallow with large, pale pink flowers with notched petals; the upper leaves are deeply cut into narrow segments, unlike Common Mallow.

name: Malva neglecta
tip: Low, spreading weed of waste ground with small, pale lilac-white flowers and rounded, shallowly lobed leaves; fruiting stalks bend down and the petals are barely longer than the sepals.

name: Malva sylvestris
tip: Tall, bushy plant of verges and waste ground, with pink-purple flowers veined darker and five-lobed leaves; petals are much longer than the sepals and are notched.

name: Tilia cordata
tip: Lime tree with small heart-shaped leaves, dark green above and blue-green beneath with rusty hair tufts in vein junctions; fragrant flowers hang under a bract. Ancient woods.

name: Tilia platyphyllos
tip: Lime tree with larger, softly hairy leaves, hairy twigs and flowers in small clusters beneath a pale bract; fruits ribbed and downy, unlike Small-leaved Lime.

name: Convallaria majalis
tip: Low woodland carpeter with two broad, ribbed oval leaves per shoot and a one-sided spray of nodding, sweet-scented white bells; fruits red berries.

name: Hyacinthoides hispanica
tip: Garden escape with broad leaves and upright, stout stem; wide open bells all round the spike, blue-purple, pink or white, with blue pollen, unlike native Bluebell.

name: Hyacinthoides non-scripta
tip: Native woodland carpet with a nodding, one-sided flower spike of narrow, deep violet-blue bells whose tips curl back and have cream pollen; sweetly scented.

name: Muscari armeniacum
tip: Garden escape on verges and waste ground with narrow, floppy leaves and a dense spike of small, rounded blue urn-shaped flowers with a white rim.

name: Ornithogalum umbellatum
tip: Bulb with narrow, grass-like leaves with a white midstripe, and starry white flowers striped green on the back; opens only in sun; garden escape in grass.

name: Ruscus aculeatus
tip: Evergreen, stiff, prickly shrub of woods and hedges; leaf-like flattened stems end in sharp spines, with tiny pale flowers in the middle and red berries.

name: Acer campestre
tip: Small tree or hedge maple with small, three- to five-lobed rounded leaves and corky-ridged twigs; upright green flower clusters; fruits have horizontally spread wings.

name: Acer platanoides
tip: Maple with sharply pointed lobes and bright yellow-green flower clusters appearing before the leaves in spring; milky sap in the leaf stalk and widely spread fruit wings.

name: Acer pseudoplatanus
tip: Large tree with big, five-lobed, coarsely toothed leaves and hanging spikes of yellow-green flowers; paired winged fruits spread at a narrow angle.

name: Aesculus carnea
tip: Planted tree like Horse-chestnut but with deep pink-red flowers in candles, dark leaflets and smoother fruits lacking strong spines.

name: Aesculus hippocastanum
tip: Large tree with big hand-shaped leaves of five to seven leaflets, sticky buds and upright candles of white flowers spotted red or yellow; spiky conkers.

name: Buddleja davidii
tip: Shrub of walls, railways and waste ground with long, arching cones of fragrant lilac-purple flowers, narrow pointed leaves white-felted beneath, loved by butterflies.

name: Scrophularia auriculata
tip: Tall, stout wetland figwort with winged square stems, rounded blunt-toothed leaves and small brown-purple flowers with a green sepal rim; flower scale lacks purple, unlike Common Figwort.

name: Scrophularia nodosa
tip: Woodland and hedgerow figwort with square, unwinged stems, pointed toothed leaves and small, red-brown globular flowers with a green lip; root has knobbly tubers.

name: Verbascum nigrum
tip: Slender mullein with a long unbranched spike of yellow flowers with violet hairy stamens; leaves green and not felted, lower ones heart-shaped at base.

name: Verbascum thapsus
tip: Tall, grey-felted biennial with a stout spike and thick white woolly leaves forming a large rosette; pale yellow flat flowers of dry soils.

name: Chrysosplenium alternifolium
tip: Small damp-woodland plant with leaves alternate on the stem, kidney-shaped and hairy, with yellow-green bracts around tiny flowers; rarer than the opposite-leaved species.

name: Chrysosplenium oppositifolium
tip: Mat-forming plant of streamsides and wet woods with paired, rounded, fleshy leaves and flat clusters of tiny golden-green flowers amid yellowish leaf-like bracts.

name: Saxifraga granulata
tip: Grassland plant with kidney-shaped, blunt-lobed hairy leaves, small bulbils at the base, and loose heads of large white flowers veined green; flowers held on tall stems.

name: Saxifraga tridactylites
tip: Tiny, sticky-hairy annual of walls and bare ground with three-lobed leaves often turning red and small white flowers with notched petals.

name: Tellima grandiflora
tip: Garden escape in woods and verges with rounded, hairy, scalloped leaves like a Heuchera and spikes of green bells whose fringed petals turn pink.

name: Crassula helmsii
tip: Invasive pond plant forming dense mats of paired, narrow, fleshy leaves; tiny four-petalled white flowers appear singly on leaf axils, often in water or on mud.

name: Sedum acre
tip: Mat-forming succulent of dunes, walls and dry grassland with tiny, fleshy, scale-like overlapping leaves tasting peppery, and star-like yellow flowers.

name: Sedum album
tip: Mat-forming succulent with small, cylindrical, bright green leaves often tinged red, and flat clusters of tiny white star flowers; walls and rocks.

name: Sedum anglicum
tip: Low succulent of rocks, dunes and coastal cliffs with small, egg-shaped, grey-green leaves often reddish, with white-pink star flowers, pink-backed.

name: Umbilicus rupestris
tip: Succulent of walls, rocks and hedgebanks with round, dimpled, scalloped leaves like little saucers and a spike of drooping greenish-white tubular flowers.

name: Datura stramonium
tip: Rank, foul-smelling annual of waste ground with large trumpet-shaped white or purplish flowers and spiny, egg-shaped seed capsules; poisonous, with coarsely toothed leaves.

name: Lycium barbarum
tip: Lax, spiny-tipped shrub of hedges and waste ground with narrow grey-green leaves, small purple funnel-shaped flowers and orange-red berries.

name: Solanum dulcamara
tip: Scrambling woody climber of hedges and wetlands with purple flowers with bent-back petals around a yellow cone, and oval red berries; leaves often eared at base.

name: Solanum nigrum
tip: Weed of cultivated land with small white flowers with yellow centres, drooping in clusters, and green then black berries; leaves are wavy-toothed oval, unlike Bittersweet.

name: Solanum tuberosum
tip: Crop plant sometimes found on tips and field edges, with pinnate leaves of uneven leaflets and clusters of white or pale purple star-like flowers with yellow centres.

name: Equisetum arvense
tip: Common weed with separate early pinkish fertile spring stems, then green sterile stems with simple whorled branches; sheaths have teeth, branches solid and ridged.

name: Equisetum fluviatile
tip: Horsetail of ponds and ditch edges with smooth, hollow, pale green stems with thin sheaths and branches few or none; fertile cones borne at tips of ordinary stems.

name: Equisetum palustre
tip: Horsetail of damp ground with grooved stems having wide black-edged sheath teeth with a white margin, and branches either absent or whorled; slender and spreading.

name: Equisetum sylvaticum
tip: Elegant horsetail of damp woodlands with feathery, repeatedly branched whorls that droop; sheaths on main stem are loose and reddish-brown, with fused teeth.

name: Equisetum telmateia
tip: Very large, robust horsetail of springs and wet banks; pale unbranched fertile stems in spring, later tall white-green stems with many dense, fine whorled branches.

name: Sparganium angustifolium
tip: Aquatic bur-reed of acid lakes with long floating ribbon-like leaves and a few unbranched, stalkless female heads; fruit beaked; zig-zag stem rising slightly above the water.

name: Sparganium emersum
tip: Bur-reed of slow rivers and ditches with keeled, triangular leaves in the lower part, unbranched flower stem, and a mix of male and female heads along it.

name: Sparganium erectum
tip: Tall marginal plant of ponds and ditches with stiff sword-like leaves and a branched flower spike carrying spiky round green heads, later burr-like.

name: Typha angustifolia
tip: Tall marginal plant with narrow, grey-green leaves and slender brown cigar-shaped catkin, with a clear gap between the upper male and lower female parts.

name: Typha latifolia
tip: Tall marginal plant of ponds with broad blue-green leaves and thick, dark brown sausage-shaped female flower spike touching the male part above it.

name: Calystegia pulchra
tip: Climber with large pink flowers, often with white stripes, and hairy stems; bracts under the flower do not overlap the sepals, and stems often hairy, unlike Hedge Bindweed.

name: Calystegia sepium
tip: Twining climber of hedges and wasteland with large white trumpets, arrow-shaped leaves, and bracteoles that are small and do not hide the sepals; hairless stems.

name: Calystegia silvatica
tip: Vigorous garden escape with large white or pink-flushed trumpets whose big bracts overlap and swell around the base of the flower; leaves broadly arrow-shaped.

name: Convolvulus arvensis
tip: Trailing or climbing weed of fields and verges with small, scented pink or white funnels often striped, and small arrow-shaped leaves; bracts are tiny and far below the flower.

name: Crocus tommasinianus
tip: Garden crocus naturalised on lawns and verges, with slender silvery-lilac flowers with pointed petals and grass-like leaves with a white stripe; flowers very early.

name: Crocus vernus
tip: Crocus naturalised in grass with large, goblet-shaped purple or white flowers with a throat that is often hairy; leaves narrow with a pale central stripe, flowering in early spring.

name: Iris foetidissima
tip: Evergreen iris of woods and scrub, with dull purplish-yellow flowers and a smell of roast beef from crushed leaves; seed pods split to show bright orange-red seeds.

name: Iris pseudacorus
tip: Tall wetland iris with sword-like leaves and bright yellow flowers; found along ponds, ditches and marshes, and flowers larger than any other yellow wetland plants.

name: Oxalis acetosella
tip: Delicate woodland plant with clover-like, heart-shaped drooping leaflets and nodding white flowers with purple veins on slender stalks; leaves fold at night.

name: Oxalis articulata
tip: Garden escape with clover-like leaves on hairy stalks from a rhizome and heads of bright pink flowers with darker veins; found on verges and waste ground.

name: Oxalis corniculata
tip: Creeping weed of paths and gardens with clover-like green or purple leaves and small yellow flowers; stipules are present and the stems root at nodes.

name: Oxalis exilis
tip: Very small, creeping New Zealand plant of lawns and paths with tiny clover-like leaves and single small yellow flowers; leaves have no purple tinge.

name: Parietaria judaica
tip: Bushy perennial of walls and rocks with reddish, softly hairy stems and alternate, untoothed oval leaves; tiny clustered green flowers in leaf axils, no stings.

name: Soleirolia soleirolii
tip: Mat-forming evergreen of damp walls and paths with tiny, rounded, bright green leaves on creeping hairy stems and almost invisible flowers in the leaf axils.

name: Urtica dioica
tip: Familiar stinging perennial with opposite, heart-based toothed leaves and drooping green catkin-like flower clusters; the stinging hairs are on both stem and leaves.

name: Urtica urens
tip: Smaller, bushy annual nettle of cultivated ground with paired, deeply toothed oval leaves and short stalked flower clusters; stings strongly; shorter than Common Nettle.

name: Ribes nigrum
tip: Shrub with strongly aromatic, yellow-gland-dotted, lobed leaves and hanging spikes of dull greenish bells; black berries; escapes in damp woods and hedges.

name: Ribes rubrum
tip: Shrub with unscented lobed leaves and drooping spikes of tiny green flowers; shiny red berries in strings; found in wet woods and hedges, with no spines.

name: Ribes sanguineum
tip: Garden shrub often seen in hedges and waste ground, with hanging clusters of bright pink-red flowers appearing before the leaves; strongly scented leaves.

name: Ribes uva-crispa
tip: Spiny shrub of hedges and woods with small lobed leaves and green-pink flowers hanging singly or in twos; fruits are hairy or smooth green berries.

name: Armeria maritima
tip: Cushion-forming plant of cliffs, saltmarsh and mountains with dense tufts of narrow grassy leaves and round heads of pink flowers on leafless stalks.

name: Claytonia perfoliata
tip: Annual with a round stem leaf cupping the tiny white flowers like a collar; spring weed of sandy cultivated ground and gardens, unlike the pink-flowered Pink Purslane.

name: Claytonia sibirica
tip: Succulent annual or biennial with a pair of separate stem leaves below pink, white-veined flowers; damp shady places, woods and gardens, not the single collar of Springbeauty.

name: Montia fontana
tip: Tiny, pale green, bright, spreading plant of wet springs, flushes and seepages with minute white flowers and opposite spoon-shaped leaves; much smaller than the purslanes.

name: Elodea canadensis
tip: Submerged plant with whorls of three blunt, rather broad dark leaves that curve back; leaves widest near the middle and less pointed than in Nuttalls Waterweed.

name: Elodea nuttallii
tip: Submerged plant with whorls of three narrow, pointed, strongly curved leaves, paler and softer than Canadian Waterweed; common in ponds and canals, spreading in recent decades.

name: Lagarosiphon major
tip: Submerged plant with leaves spirally arranged, crowded and strongly curled backwards, giving a bottlebrush look; stiff stems, unlike the whorled leaves of Elodea. Garden pond escape.

name: Fraxinus excelsior
tip: Tall tree with opposite pinnate leaves, grey furrowed bark and black buds in winter; flowers appear before the leaves, followed by bunches of winged keys.

name: Ligustrum vulgare
tip: Semi-evergreen shrub with opposite, narrow dark glossy smooth-edged leaves and heavy-scented creamy flower spikes, followed by shiny black berries; on chalk and limestone scrub.

name: Syringa vulgaris
tip: Large garden shrub or small tree with opposite heart-shaped leaves and dense, sweetly scented lilac or white flower clusters in spring; naturalised on hedges and old sites.

name: Berberis vulgaris
tip: Spiny shrub with three-pronged spines and clusters of small leaves; hanging yellow flower sprays in May and red berries; hedgerows, unlike evergreen Oregon-grape.

name: Mahonia aquifolium
tip: Evergreen shrub with glossy holly-like pinnate leaves and dense upright yellow flower clusters in early spring; later blue-black berries. Planted and naturalised, no spines on stem.

name: Botrychium lunaria
tip: Small fern with a single half-moon shaped pinnae on a fleshy frond and a separate spore spike; short turf, dunes and grassland, often hard to spot.

name: Ophioglossum vulgatum
tip: Small fern with one oval, undivided green blade and a spore spike rising from its base like a snake tongue; damp meadows and old grassland.

name: Cornus sanguinea
tip: Shrub with opposite oval leaves with curved veins, dark red autumn colour and winter twigs; white flower clusters in summer and black berries; hedges on chalk and clay.

name: Cornus sericea
tip: Suckering shrub with bright red winter stems, grown for colour and naturalised in damp ground; fruits white, unlike black berries of native Dogwood.

name: Euonymus europaeus
tip: Shrub with green square-ish twigs, opposite finely toothed leaves and bright pink four-lobed fruits opening to orange seeds; hedges and scrub on chalk and limestone.

name: Parnassia palustris
tip: White five-petalled flower with green veins, fan of false stamens, on a stem with single clasping leaf; wet, peaty and calcareous flushes, late summer. Not a grass.

name: Frangula alnus
tip: Thornless shrub with alternate smooth-edged leaves, straight veins and berries ripening red to black; wet woods and heaths, unlike thorny, toothed-leaved Purging Buckthorn.

name: Rhamnus cathartica
tip: Often thorn-tipped shrub with finely toothed oval leaves in curved veins, opposite buds and black berries; on chalk and limestone scrub, unlike thornless Alder Buckthorn.

name: Hedera helix
tip: Evergreen climber with lobed leaves on creeping stems and unlobed on flowering stems; round green-yellow umbels in autumn feed insects, followed by black berries.

name: Hydrocotyle vulgaris
tip: Creeping plant of bogs and wet ground with round, shield-like scalloped leaves on long stalks; flowers tiny and hidden beneath. Not related to Navelwort.

name: Huperzia selago
tip: Erect, forked tufts of crowded stiff, pointed leaves with yellowish bulbils at tips; no cones; upland heath, rock ledges and mountain grassland.

name: Lycopodium clavatum
tip: Creeping clubmoss with leaves bearing a white hair tip and spore cones on slim stalks in pairs; heaths and moors, unlike erect Fir Clubmoss.

name: Juniperus communis
tip: Prickly conifer shrub with needles in threes, each with a white stripe above, and berry-like cones turning blue-black; chalk downs, moors and uplands.

name: Thuja plicata
tip: Large conifer with flat sprays of scale-like glossy leaves smelling of pineapple when crushed and small upright cones; widely planted in forestry and parks.

name: Linum catharticum
tip: Slender annual with tiny white four-to-five-petalled flowers and opposite narrow leaves; chalk and limestone grassland, dunes, short turf, unlike cultivated blue Flax.

name: Linum usitatissimum
tip: Tall slender annual with bright blue flowers, narrow alternate leaves and rounded seed capsules; relic of cultivation on waste ground and field edges.

name: Lythrum portula
tip: Small creeping annual of wet muddy places with opposite spoon-shaped leaves and tiny stalkless flowers in leaf axils; flowers are easily overlooked.

name: Lythrum salicaria
tip: Tall plant of wet places with leafy spikes of vivid magenta flowers and opposite or whorled narrow leaves, in summer; unlike willowherbs, has six petals.

name: Menyanthes trifoliata
tip: Wetland plant with three-leaflet leaves and spikes of white to pink fringed star-like flowers; shallow water, bogs and fens in spring.

name: Nymphoides peltata
tip: Floating plant with small water-lily-like heart-shaped leaves and yellow five-petalled fringed flowers held above water; ponds and slow rivers, not a true water-lily.

name: Myriophyllum alterniflorum
tip: Submerged plant with feathery whorled leaves, flower spike tip often drooping and flowers alternately arranged; in acid, peaty waters, unlike coarser Spiked Water-milfoil.

name: Myriophyllum spicatum
tip: Submerged plant with feathery leaves in whorls of four and more than 13 pairs of thread-like segments; erect red-tinged flower spikes in hard, base-rich water.

name: Nuphar lutea
tip: Floating oval leaves with notch at base and rounded yellow ball-like flowers held at the surface, smelling of alcohol; ponds, canals and slow rivers.

name: Nymphaea alba
tip: Large white flowers with many petals and yellow centre floating on round, deeply notched leaves; lakes and ponds, bigger and whiter than any other native water plant.

name: Polygala serpyllifolia
tip: Small, wiry plant with lower leaves opposite, small blue, pink or white flowers; acid heaths and grassland, unlike Common Milkwort, leaves all alternate.

name: Polygala vulgaris
tip: Low plant with all leaves alternate, narrow, and spikes of small blue, pink or white flowers; chalk and neutral grassland, versus Heath Milkwort.

name: Reseda lutea
tip: Biennial or perennial with deeply cut leaves and dense spikes of small pale yellow flowers; chalk and disturbed ground, unlike the undivided leaves of Weld.

name: Reseda luteola
tip: Tall biennial with a basal rosette and narrow undivided wavy-edged leaves; long slender spikes of small yellowish-green flowers on waste ground.

name: Triglochin maritima
tip: Grass-like plant of saltmarsh with fleshy narrow leaves and tall spikes of small green flowers, fruit with six parts; coastal, versus Marsh Arrowgrass inland.

name: Triglochin palustris
tip: Grass-like plant of freshwater marshes and fens with slender flower spike and fruit splitting into three parts at the base; inland, unlike Sea Arrowgrass.

name: Ulmus glabra
tip: Large tree with very large rough leaves with a short stalk, often lopsided and with overlapping base lobes, and no suckers; winged fruits with central seed.

name: Ulmus minor
tip: Suckering elm with smaller smooth to slightly rough leaves, asymmetric at base, often forming hedgerows; highly variable and difficult to separate from relatives.

name: Verbena bonariensis
tip: Tall, wiry, branched plant with square stems, narrow rough toothed leaves and flat clusters of small purple flowers; garden escape, now on waste ground and verges.

name: Verbena officinalis
tip: Wiry plant with deeply lobed lower leaves and thin spikes of tiny pale lilac flowers; dry grassland, roadsides and waste ground.

name: Vinca major
tip: Large trailing evergreen with big blue flowers and heart-shaped, hairy-edged leaves; bigger than Lesser Periwinkle with sepals fringed, in hedges and banks.

name: Vinca minor
tip: Trailing evergreen with smaller glossy narrow oval leaves and blue flowers, calyx hairless; woodland and hedge banks, smaller than Greater Periwinkle.

name: Azolla filiculoides
tip: Tiny floating fern forming a red or green mat of overlapping scale-like leaves on still water; introduced, often turning red in autumn.

name: Bryonia dioica
tip: Climbing hedge plant with tendrils, palmately lobed rough leaves and greenish-white flowers, followed by red berries; the only British climber with tendrils in this family.

name: Butomus umbellatus
tip: Tall plant of water margins with narrow triangular leaves and umbels of pink flowers on a tall stem; not a rush, summer.

name: Buxus sempervirens
tip: Evergreen shrub with small opposite glossy oval leaves; tiny greenish-yellow flowers in clusters in spring; native on chalk slopes, widely planted in hedges.

name: Ceratophyllum demersum
tip: Submerged rootless plant with stiff dark green whorled forked leaves with tiny teeth; flowers seldom seen, in still and slow water.

name: Daphne laureola
tip: Evergreen shrub with glossy, leathery oval leaves in tufts at the shoot tips, small green flowers, and black berries; shaded woods on calcareous soils, winter flowering.

name: Drosera rotundifolia
tip: Insect-eating plant of bogs with a rosette of round red sticky-haired leaves; small white flowers on a slender spike, summer, in acid wet moors.

name: Helianthemum nummularium
tip: Low spreading evergreen with bright yellow, crumpled-petal flowers and opposite narrow oval leaves, white beneath; sunny chalk grassland and rocks.

name: Hippophae rhamnoides
tip: Thorny coastal shrub with narrow silvery leaves and dense bunches of orange berries in autumn; dunes and sea cliffs, sometimes spreading inland.

name: Humulus lupulus
tip: Climbing twining plant of hedges with rough lobed leaves and green papery cones on female plants; grows clockwise, flowering summer.

name: Ilex aquifolium
tip: Evergreen tree or shrub with glossy spiny leaves, though upper leaves are sometimes smooth; small white flowers and red berries on female trees.

name: Impatiens glandulifera
tip: Very tall annual with pink-purple hooded flowers, whorled leaves with red stems, and exploding seed pods; common on riverbanks, strongly scented.

name: Juglans regia
tip: Large tree with aromatic pinnate leaves with 5 to 9 leaflets and long green catkins; planted and self-sown near fruiting trees, with big green-husked nuts.

name: Myrica gale
tip: Fragrant low shrub of wet heaths and bogs with aromatic grey-green leaves and reddish catkins before the leaves appear; crush leaf to smell resin.

name: Narthecium ossifragum
tip: Tufts of flat iris-like leaves and spikes of star-shaped yellow flowers with orange anthers on wet moors and bogs; orange fruit follows.

name: Osmunda regalis
tip: Tall fern with twice-pinnate fronds, rounded leaflets, and brown spore clusters at the frond tip; wet woods and bogs, large and distinctive.

name: Parthenocissus quinquefolia
tip: Climbing vine with leaves of five leaflets and tendrils with sticky pads, turning scarlet in autumn; garden escape on walls and hedges.

name: Pinguicula vulgaris
tip: Sticky yellow-green rosette of rolled-edge leaves trapping insects, with single violet flower on a leafless stalk; wet moors, bogs and flushes.

name: Pteridium aquilinum
tip: Very tall coarse fern forming dense stands from creeping rhizomes with large triangular fronds, dying brown in autumn; heaths, hillsides and woods.

name: Rhus typhina
tip: Suckering small tree with velvety stems and long pinnate leaves turning red in autumn; dense red conical fruit heads; planted in gardens and escaping.

name: Selaginella selaginoides
tip: Small moss-like creeping plant with soft, spreading bristly-toothed leaves and an upright cone; damp flushes in upland grassland and dune slacks.

name: Tamus communis
tip: Twining climber of hedges with glossy heart-shaped leaves and tiny green flowers; red berries in autumn. Climbs anticlockwise with no tendrils, unlike White Bryony.

name: Taxus baccata
tip: Evergreen conifer with flat dark green needles, red cup-like fleshy arils around the seed, and reddish flaking bark; woods, churchyards and chalk slopes.

name: Viscum album
tip: Evergreen parasitic shrub forming round balls on tree branches, with paired yellow-green oval leaves and white berries; on apple, lime and poplar.

name: Chamaenerion angustifolium
tip: Tall stands of magenta flower spikes on waste ground, clearings and railways; long narrow leaves arranged spirally; seeds with white fluff in late summer.

name: Bistorta officinalis
tip: Dense pink poker-like spikes on unbranched stems above broad, triangular-based leaves with winged stalks; damp meadows, often in patches.

name: Bistorta vivipara
tip: Upland grassland; slender spike of white or pale pink flowers, the lower part replaced by small purplish bulbils; narrow leaves.

name: Reynoutria japonica
tip: Dense thickets of zigzag, bamboo-like red-speckled stems with broad leaves cut straight across at the base; sprays of creamy flowers in autumn.

name: Erythranthe guttata
tip: Streamsides; large bright yellow two-lipped snapdragon-like flowers, often with small red spots in the throat; opposite toothed leaves.

name: Helosciadium nodiflorum
tip: Sprawling in shallow water and ditches; pinnate leaves with toothed leaflets like watercress; small white umbels on short stalks opposite the leaves.

name: Helosciadium inundatum
tip: Small plant of pond edges and shallow water with thread-like submerged leaves, pinnate upper leaves and tiny umbels of two or three rays.

name: Hylotelephium telephium
tip: Fleshy grey-green oval toothed leaves on upright stems, topped by dense flat heads of reddish-purple starry flowers; woodland edges and hedgebanks.

name: Lysimachia arvensis
tip: Low sprawling annual of bare and cultivated ground; small orange-red five-petalled flowers that close in dull weather; opposite unstalked oval leaves dotted beneath.

name: Lysimachia tenella
tip: Creeping mats in wet acid ground with tiny round paired leaves and delicate pale pink bell-shaped flowers on long thin stalks.

name: Lysimachia maritima
tip: Low fleshy plant of saltmarshes and coastal rocks; small pink flowers with no petals, sitting in the leaf joints; opposite oval leaves.

name: Lysimachia minima
tip: Minute annual of damp bare sandy or peaty ground, often under 5 cm; tiny pinkish flowers hidden in the leaf joints.

name: Lysimachia europaea
tip: Northern woods and moors; a single whorl of shiny leaves at the top of a slender stem with one or two starry white flowers of about seven petals.

name: Stellaria aquatica
tip: Like a large straggling chickweed of wet ground and riverbanks, with heart-based leaves and white flowers whose petals are split almost to the base, five styles.

name: Stuckenia pectinata
tip: Submerged pondweed with very narrow thread-like leaves fanning out from long sheaths, and short interrupted flower spikes; ponds, canals and brackish water.

name: Stuckenia filiformis
tip: Like Fennel Pondweed but smaller with fine thread-like leaves in clear northern lakes, often in sand; flower spike long and widely interrupted.

name: Cupressus lawsoniana
tip: Planted conifer with flattened sprays of tiny scale leaves that smell of parsley when crushed, a drooping leading shoot and small round cones.

name: Ervilia hirsuta
tip: Slender scrambling vetch with many pairs of narrow leaflets ending in tendrils and tiny pale lilac flowers; pods hairy with two seeds.

name: Ervum tetraspermum
tip: Like Hairy Tare but flowers slightly larger, pale lilac, one or two together, and the pods hairless with about four seeds.

name: Linum radiola
tip: Tiny branched annual of damp acid sandy tracks with paired oval leaves and many minute white four-petalled flowers.

name: Micranthes stellaris
tip: Upland streamsides and wet rocks; rosettes of toothed leaves and starry white flowers with two yellow spots on each petal and red anthers.

name: Rhodiola rosea
tip: Sea cliffs and mountain ledges; fleshy grey-blue leaves densely clothing thick stems topped by heads of yellowish flowers; roots smell of roses.

name: Oxybasis rubra
tip: Fleshy, often red-tinged goosefoot of manure heaps, pond margins and saltmarsh edges with diamond-shaped toothed leaves and dense green flower spikes.

name: Blitum bonus-henricus
tip: Farmyards and roadsides; mealy, broad triangular arrow-shaped leaves and tall leafless spikes of tiny greenish flowers.

name: Sabulina verna
tip: Low tufts of short narrow leaves on limestone, lead-mine spoil and mountain ledges, covered in starry white five-petalled flowers.

name: Achillea millefolium
tip: Flat-topped clusters of tiny white or pinkish daisies over feathery, finely divided dark green leaves with an aromatic smell. Common in grassland and verges, summer to autumn.

name: Achillea ptarmica
tip: Like yarrow but with undivided, narrow, sharply saw-edged leaves and fewer, larger creamy white heads with a greenish centre. Damp meadows, rushy pastures and moorland edges.

name: Antennaria dioica
tip: Low mat with white woolly spoon-shaped leaves and short stalks of papery pink or white button heads that never open as daisies. Upland grassland and heath.

name: Arctium lappa
tip: Large burdock with big heart-shaped leaves and long-stalked heads in a loose flat-topped cluster; bracts have hooked tips. Told from Lesser Burdock by larger heads and solid leaf stalks.

name: Arctium minus
tip: Burdock with stalkless or short-stalked heads in a spike-like arrangement, smaller than Greater Burdock, and hooked bracts that cling to clothing. Hollow leaf stalks; waste ground and hedgerows.

name: Arctium nemorosum
tip: Burdock with heads on long stalks and bracts whose hooks are purple-tinged, mostly in woodland edges and shady verges. Heads often smaller and more open than Greater Burdock; tricky to separate.

name: Artemisia vulgaris
tip: Tall, tough plant with dark green deeply cut leaves that are silvery-white beneath, and long spikes of small dull reddish-brown button heads. Waste ground, verges, late summer.

name: Bellis perennis
tip: Familiar lawn plant with a flat rosette of spoon-shaped leaves and single white-rayed, yellow-centred heads on leafless stalks. Flowers nearly all year.

name: Bidens cernua
tip: Yellow heads nodding on the stem, often without rays, over unlobed toothed opposite leaves. Wet margins of ponds and ditches, late summer; seeds have barbed bristles.

name: Bidens tripartita
tip: Opposite leaves usually cut into three lobes, and upright, rayless dull yellow heads with leafy bracts. Pond edges and ditches; barbed seeds stick to clothing.

name: Calendula officinalis
tip: Garden escape with bright orange or yellow large daisy heads, rather fleshy aromatic sticky leaves and curved ridged seeds. Found on tips, waste ground and field edges.

name: Carduus crispus
tip: Slender thistle whose stems are winged right up to the heads with wavy spiny wings, and small clustered purple heads. Verges and rough grass in summer.

name: Carduus nutans
tip: Big nodding purple heads with broad spreading spiny bracts, and spiny-winged stems below. Grows on chalk and limestone grassland and disturbed ground, summer.

name: Carlina vulgaris
tip: Stiff, spiny, small thistle with straw-coloured, shiny bracts spreading like rays around a brown centre; dead heads persist through winter. Dry chalk and limestone grassland.

name: Centaurea cyanus
tip: Slender grey-green plant with bright blue heads whose outer florets are large and spreading. Arable field edges, wasteland and sown wildflower strips, summer.

name: Centaurea debeauxii
tip: Slender knapweed with deeply cut stem leaves and rather small purple heads with narrow, pale-fringed bracts. Chalk grassland in southern England; hard to separate from Common Knapweed.

name: Centaurea montana
tip: Garden escape with large blue heads whose outer florets are spreading, and bracts edged with black fringes. Leaves are broad and unlobed; found on verges and waste ground.

name: Centaurea nigra
tip: Purple thistle-like heads with dark brown, comb-fringed bracts forming a rounded knob, over unlobed or slightly lobed leaves. Abundant in grassland; no spines.

name: Centaurea scabiosa
tip: Larger knapweed with deeply cut leaves and heads with black-tipped bracts that are not a dark mop; outer florets are enlarged. Dry calcareous grassland.

name: Cicerbita macrophylla
tip: Tall hairy plant with pale blue-violet dandelion-like heads and large leaves with a big triangular end lobe. Escaped from gardens to damp shady verges and woodland edges.

name: Cichorium intybus
tip: Tall, stiff, branching plant with bright sky-blue dandelion-like heads that open in the morning, stalkless along the stems. Dry grassland, verges and field edges.

name: Cirsium acaule
tip: Stemless thistle with a flat rosette of spiny leaves and one or more big purple heads sitting at ground level. Short chalk and limestone turf.

name: Cirsium arvense
tip: Common spreading thistle with lilac, scented heads in clusters, stems not winged and leaves spiny but only slightly cottony. Forms patches in fields and verges.

name: Cirsium heterophyllum
tip: Spineless thistle with unlobed, lance-shaped leaves white and felted beneath, clasping the stem, and a single large drooping purple head. Upland meadows and verges.

name: Cirsium palustre
tip: Tall, narrow thistle with spiny-winged stems and dense clusters of small purple heads at the top. Damp meadows, rushy pasture and heaths.

name: Cirsium vulgare
tip: Large heads on a spiny-winged stem, with fierce spear-shaped spiny leaves that are bristly above. Common on grassland and waste ground, late summer.

name: Crepis biennis
tip: Tall hairy biennial with large golden heads and toothed, lobed leaves; outer bracts are bristly and the buds nod. Meadows and verges, early summer.

name: Crepis capillaris
tip: Small yellow dandelion-like heads in loose clusters, orange-red beneath, over mostly smooth leaves with arrow-shaped stem leaf bases. Lawns, walls, verges; flowers until late autumn.

name: Crepis paludosa
tip: Leafy plant of damp places with unlobed or little-lobed clasping stem leaves and orange-yellow heads, black-hairy bracts. Wet meadows and streamsides, northern and western Britain.

name: Crepis vesicaria
tip: Hairy plant with deeply cut leaves and yellow heads, outer florets orange-streaked beneath; fruits have a beak. Roadsides, walls and waste ground, mainly southern England.

name: Doronicum pardalianches
tip: Early-flowering plant with large yellow daisies and big heart-shaped basal leaves, clasping stem leaves. Naturalised in woods and shady verges, spring and early summer.

name: Erigeron acris
tip: Small daisy with thin lilac-purple rays and a yellow disc, hairy erect stem, narrow leaves. Dry grassland, walls and dunes on calcareous ground.

name: Erigeron canadensis
tip: Tall, bristly, much-branched weed with masses of tiny whitish heads whose rays barely show. Waste ground, pavements and railway land, summer to autumn.

name: Erigeron karvinskianus
tip: Wall-colonising daisy with white rays turning pink and yellow centres, often with three-lobed leaves. Flowers for months on walls, steps and rocks.

name: Eupatorium cannabinum
tip: Tall plant with flat-topped clusters of tiny pale pink fluffy heads over hairy, palmately lobed opposite leaves. Wet places, fens and ditches, late summer.

name: Galinsoga quadriradiata
tip: Weed of gardens and arable land with tiny daisies of five short white rays and a yellow centre, opposite leaves, hairy stems. Distinguished from Gallant-soldier by hairier stems.

name: Glebionis segetum
tip: Bright yellow large daisy with greyish, toothed to lobed hairless leaves clasping the stem. Arable fields and waste ground, summer.

name: Gnaphalium uliginosum
tip: Low grey woolly plant with clusters of dull brownish-yellow heads at stem tops, surrounded by leaves. Damp bare ground in tracks, fields and gardens.

name: Helminthotheca echioides
tip: Coarse, bristly plant with warty-based bristles on leaves and yellow dandelion-like heads, bracts heart-shaped and leafy. Verges, field edges and waste ground.

name: Hieracium sabaudum
tip: Leafy hawkweed with many narrow-ish toothed stem leaves and clusters of yellow heads in late summer. Woods, hedgebanks and heathy places; hawkweeds are hard to identify precisely.

name: Hieracium umbellatum
tip: Leafy hawkweed with many narrow, nearly stalkless leaves up the stem and a flat-topped umbel of yellow heads. Heaths, dry woodland edges and railway banks.

name: Hypochaeris radicata
tip: Dandelion-like but with branched, nearly leafless stems bearing small scale-like bracts and a flat rosette of hairy, lobed leaves. Grassland and lawns, summer.

name: Inula conyzae
tip: Tall, sticky-hairy, aromatic plant with rather dull yellowish-brown button heads with short rays, and broad woolly leaves. Dry chalk and limestone scrub and banks.

name: Jacobaea aquatica
tip: Ragwort of wet places with hairless, little-divided leaves and a broad top; yellow rays spread rather than hang down. Ditches, wet meadows and fens.

name: Jacobaea erucifolia
tip: Ragwort with narrow-lobed leaves white and cottony beneath, and flat-topped yellow heads. Grassy places on chalk and roadsides, mainly south-east England.

name: Jacobaea vulgaris
tip: Branched ragwort with ragged, deeply cut leaves and flat-topped clusters of yellow daisies. Very common on grassland and waste ground; poisonous to livestock.

name: Lactuca serriola
tip: Tall, greyish lettuce with leaves twisted to face north-south, prickles along the midrib beneath, and small pale yellow heads. Waste ground and walls.

name: Lactuca virosa
tip: Tall robust lettuce with big undivided, broad leaves held horizontally and small pale yellow heads in a large pyramid. Waste ground, chalk and coasts; purplish stem.

name: Lapsana communis
tip: Slender, branched plant with many small pale yellow heads that open only in the morning, and fruits with no hairy parachute. Hedgebanks, walls and waste places.

name: Leontodon hispidus
tip: Rosette plant with bristly leaves with forked hairs and single yellow dandelion-like heads on unbranched, leafy-scale stalks. Grassland, mostly on chalk and lime.

name: Leontodon saxatilis
tip: Small, slender plant with hairless or sparsely hairy leaves, drooping buds and small yellow heads that are red-striped beneath. Short grass, lawns and coastal turf.

name: Leucanthemum vulgare
tip: Large white daisy with yellow centre on tall stems, and rounded toothed spoon-shaped basal leaves. Common in meadows and verges, summer.

name: Matricaria chamomilla
tip: Finely divided feathery leaves smelling sweetly of apples, and small white-rayed daisies with a cone-shaped hollow yellow centre. Arable land and waste ground.

name: Matricaria discoidea
tip: Greenish-yellow rayless button heads, feathery leaves that smell of pineapple when crushed. Trampled ground, gateways and paths.

name: Mycelis muralis
tip: Slender, hairless plant with a loose spray of tiny heads of only five yellow florets and leaves with a large terminal lobe. Shady walls and woodland.

name: Omalotheca sylvatica
tip: Upright, grey-woolly plant with narrow leaves and a spike of small brown-tipped heads in leaf axils. Open heathy ground and tracks.

name: Onopordum acanthium
tip: Huge, silvery-woolly thistle with broad spiny wings on the stem and large purple heads. Waste ground, field edges and roadsides, mainly eastern England.

name: Petasites hybridus
tip: Early spikes of pale pink flower heads appear before giant, rhubarb-like round leaves. Wet verges and riverbanks.

name: Picris hieracioides
tip: Tall, bristly plant with unlobed narrow leaves and yellow dandelion-like heads with dark bristly bracts, on branching stems. Dry grassland and banks, mostly on chalk.

name: Pilosella aurantiaca
tip: Orange-red dandelion-like heads, several to a stem, with black-hairy bracts and hairy rosette leaves. Garden escape on grassy banks, walls and verges.

name: Pilosella officinarum
tip: Low mat-forming plant with silvery-white, felted leaf undersides and pale lemon, single heads, red-striped beneath. Dry banks, walls and short turf.

name: Pulicaria dysenterica
tip: Hairy plant with wavy-edged, clasping leaves and flat-topped clusters of golden, rather narrow-rayed daisies. Damp meadows, ditches and wet roadsides.

name: Scorzoneroides autumnalis
tip: Slender, branched plant with scaly stems that swell below the heads and hairless, narrow, lobed leaves. Grassland and lawns, late summer into autumn.

name: Senecio inaequidens
tip: Branched ragwort with narrow, unlobed linear leaves and many small yellow daisies; invader of railways, roadsides and docks, flowering until winter.

name: Senecio squalidus
tip: Low, hairless ragwort with shiny deeply cut leaves and yellow daisies with black-tipped bracts. Walls, railways and pavements; flowers almost year-round.

name: Senecio sylvaticus
tip: Sticky-hairy groundsel with short, rolled-back rays and sticky leaves, taller and narrower than Sticky Groundsel; heaths and sandy ground.

name: Senecio viscosus
tip: Strongly sticky and smelly groundsel with rolled-back short rays, and yellow heads in leafy clusters. Disturbed ground, railway tracks and gardens.

name: Senecio vulgaris
tip: Small weed with lobed leaves and clusters of narrow yellow heads without rays, black-tipped bracts and fluffy seeds. Flowers almost all year in gardens.

name: Serratula tinctoria
tip: Thistle lookalike without spines, with purple heads in loose clusters and finely saw-toothed, often deeply lobed leaves. Damp grassland, woodland rides and heaths.

name: Solidago canadensis
tip: Tall garden escape with spiky one-sided plumes of tiny yellow heads, hairy stem upper half and three-veined leaves. Waste ground and railway banks in late summer.

name: Solidago gigantea
tip: Tall goldenrod with smooth, hairless stem, and wide-spreading plumes of small yellow heads. Naturalised on waste ground and riversides.

name: Solidago virgaurea
tip: Native goldenrod with short, upright spikes of golden daisies, leaves broader at base. Woods, heaths, cliffs, hedgebanks and rocky ground.

name: Sonchus arvensis
tip: Tall creeping plant with large golden-yellow dandelion-like heads and glandular yellow-hairy stalks, soft-spined leaves. Arable fields, ditches and coastal marshes.

name: Sonchus asper
tip: Glossy leaves with sharp spiny teeth and rounded clasping lobes at the base, and small pale yellow heads. Waste ground and gardens.

name: Sonchus oleraceus
tip: Soft sow-thistle with soft-toothed leaves whose basal lobes are pointed, and pale yellow heads. Weed of gardens and waste ground.

name: Symphyotrichum lanceolatum
tip: Garden Michaelmas-daisy with narrow lance-shaped leaves, small white to pale lilac rayed heads and many on panicles; spreads on waste ground.

name: Symphyotrichum novi-belgii
tip: Common garden escape with blue-violet daisies with yellow centres on leafy stems, found on riverbanks and waste ground in autumn.

name: Tanacetum parthenium
tip: Strongly bitter-scented plant with yellowish-green, divided leaves and clusters of small white daisies with flat yellow centres. Walls, gardens and waste ground.

name: Tanacetum vulgare
tip: Dense flat clusters of yellow button heads without rays, over dark green, finely divided leaves with strong aromatic smell. Verges and riverbanks.

name: Tragopogon pratensis
tip: Grass-like grey-green leaves and large yellow heads that close by midday, with bracts longer than the rays, and big fluffy clocks. Meadows and verges.

name: Tripleurospermum inodorum
tip: Unscented, feathery leaves and white-rayed daisies with a domed yellow solid centre; common weed of arable land and waste ground.

name: Tripleurospermum maritimum
tip: Fleshy, spreading plant of shingle and sea cliffs with thick, finely divided leaves and large white daisies. Coastal; stems often sprawling.

name: Tripolium pannonicum
tip: Fleshy-leaved plant of saltmarshes with lilac-rayed yellow-centred daisies, occasionally rayless. Grows in muddy estuaries and creeks.

name: Tussilago farfara
tip: Yellow dandelion-like flowers on scaly stems appear in early spring before the large, hoof-shaped leaves, which are white-felted beneath. Disturbed clay soils.

name: Agrostis canina
tip: Fine, tufted bent of acid grassland with a long pointed ligule and a bent awn on the lemma; spreads by leafy runners and heads contract after flowering.

name: Agrostis capillaris
tip: Very common lawn and grassland bent with a short, blunt ligule and an open airy panicle; rarely awned and slightly spreading by rhizomes.

name: Agrostis gigantea
tip: Tall, creeping bent with a long, blunt ligule and rough leaves; panicle stays open and reddish, mainly on arable margins and rough ground.

name: Agrostis stolonifera
tip: Mat-forming bent with long leafy runners and a long ligule; panicle contracts into a narrow lobed shape after flowering, in damp ground and lawns.

name: Agrostis vinealis
tip: Tufted bent of dry acid heath with a longer ligule than Common Bent and a small awn; short rhizomes and a narrow brownish panicle.

name: Aira caryophyllea
tip: Tiny annual of dry sandy ground with an airy silvery-purple panicle on hair-thin branches; spikelets bear a bent awn and the ligule is long.

name: Aira praecox
tip: Small annual with a dense, short, spike-like panicle, shiny and yellowish-green; flowers very early on dry sandy soil, with bristly hair-like leaves.

name: Alopecurus geniculatus
tip: Bristly cylindrical head with awns, found in wet ground; stems bend at the nodes and root there, and the anthers are orange, unlike Meadow Foxtail.

name: Alopecurus myosuroides
tip: Arable weed with a slender, tapering, often purplish cylindrical head; awned like other foxtails, but annual and lacking the soft downy feel of Meadow Foxtail.

name: Alopecurus pratensis
tip: Soft, pale cylindrical head resembling Timothy but with a bristle on each spikelet; flowers early in spring in meadows, with a long ligule.

name: Anisantha diandra
tip: Large drooping panicle with very long awns on big spikelets; sheaths softly hairy; spikelets longer than Barren Brome with branches rarely over 5 cm.

name: Anisantha sterilis
tip: Common roadside annual with a drooping panicle of long-awned spikelets spreading to one side; hairy sheaths and branches longer than Great Brome.

name: Anthoxanthum odoratum
tip: Smells of new-mown hay when crushed; spike-like yellowish-green head, early flowering, with a short awn on the lower lemmas and slightly hairy leaves.

name: Arrhenatherum elatius
tip: Tall tufted grass of verges with a long open panicle of shining spikelets, each with a bent awn; stem bases often swollen like beads.

name: Avena fatua
tip: Tall arable weed with large drooping oat spikelets, awned with a bent awn and a hairy base; spikelets fall whole and the ligule is long.

name: Avena sativa
tip: Cultivated cereal with large drooping spikelets, mostly awnless or with weak awns, unlike Wild-oat; spikelets do not shed readily.

name: Avenella flexuosa
tip: Tufted grass of heaths and acid woods with hair-fine wiry leaves and shiny purplish-bronze panicle; each spikelet has a bent awn.

name: Avenula pubescens
tip: Chalk grassland oat-grass with softly hairy leaves and sheaths, and large spikelets with a bent awn; ligule long and the panicle narrow.

name: Brachypodium sylvaticum
tip: Shade-loving, yellowish-green, drooping spike of short-stalked awned spikelets in woods and hedges; leaves broad, softly hairy and flopping.

name: Briza media
tip: Chalk grassland grass with heart-shaped, trembling, purplish spikelets hanging on hair-fine stalks in a loose open panicle; no awns.

name: Bromopsis erecta
tip: Chalk grassland brome with erect panicle and stiff erect branches, awned spikelets, and rolled leaves with hairs on the margins and sheaths.

name: Bromopsis ramosa
tip: Woodland brome with a drooping panicle of few long-awned spikelets and broad, hairy leaves; the sheaths bristle with spreading hairs.

name: Bromus hordeaceus
tip: Common brome with a short, dense, erect, softly downy panicle; leaves and sheaths soft with hairs, and spikelets bear short straight awns.

name: Bromus racemosus
tip: Brome of damp meadows with an erect panicle of smooth spikelets, shorter awns than Rye Brome and sheaths often hairy; spikelets not downy.

name: Bromus secalinus
tip: Annual weed of cornfields with nodding spikelets that have short, outcurved awns; spikelets are swollen and plump, becoming weakly twisted.

name: Calamagrostis epigejos
tip: Tall, creeping, tough grass with a dense, purplish-brown plume and a hairy-based bristle on each floret; leaves rough and stiff, on scrub and rough ground.

name: Catapodium marinum
tip: Stiff, short, one-sided spike of spikelets, close to the ground on rocks and sea walls; spikelets sit straight on the stem and are unawned.

name: Catapodium rigidum
tip: Small, rigid grass of dry walls and dry ground, with a triangular stiff panicle with very short branches carrying unawned spikelets.

name: Cortaderia selloana
tip: Huge garden escape forming giant clumps with silvery-white plumes up to a metre long; leaves have razor-sharp edges, ligule is a fringe of hairs.

name: Cynosurus cristatus
tip: Narrow stiff one-sided spike like a comb, shiny and green; a small awn on each spikelet and wiry flower stems; common in pasture.

name: Dactylis glomerata
tip: Coarse tufted grass with dense one-sided clusters of spikelets at the ends of branches; flattened folded shoots and long ligule.

name: Danthonia decumbens
tip: Short grass of heaths with few large spikelets in a sparse panicle, no awns, and a ligule of hairs; leaves have long hairs at the base.

name: Deschampsia cespitosa
tip: Big tussocks with very sharp-ridged leaves rough to the touch, and a large airy silvery-purple panicle of small spikelets with a short awn.

name: Echinochloa crus-galli
tip: Warm-season annual weed with a head made of several short, dense, one-sided racemes, often purplish; no ligule at all, which helps identify it.

name: Elymus athericus
tip: Stiff, bluish-green couch of salt marsh edges with a flat spike of spikelets set edge-on in two rows; leaves rolled and ribbed on top.

name: Elymus caninus
tip: Tufted couch of woods and hedges with an arching spike and long awns on the spikelets; no creeping rhizomes unlike Common Couch.

name: Elymus junceiformis
tip: Blue-grey stiff couch of foredunes with a brittle spike, spikelets overlapping and unawned; leaves rolled and ribbed above, creeping by rhizomes.

name: Elymus repens
tip: Creeping weed forming patches with a flat two-rowed spike; narrow claw-like auricles at the leaf base and white rhizomes distinguish it.

name: Festuca filiformis
tip: Bristle-leaved fescue of dry acid grassland with fine hair-thin leaves, short awns and a narrow panicle; shoots tufted, distinct from Red Fescue.

name: Festuca ovina
tip: Dense tussocks of bristle-fine bluish-green leaves on heaths and downs; small panicle with awned spikelets, leaves all rolled at the base.

name: Festuca rubra
