name: Gonocarpus micranthus
tip: Tiny creeping plant with small toothed leaves and minute greenish flowers. Naturalised from Australasia in western Scotland and Ireland. Specialist check advised.

name: Myriophyllum aquaticum
tip: Aquatic, with emergent feathery blue-green whorled leaves held above water. Female flowers are rare. Invasive in ponds and ditches across lowland Britain.

name: Myriophyllum verticillatum
tip: Submerged plant with whorled feathery leaves and flowers in whorls on a spike above the water. Bracts are longer than the flowers. Found in rich still water, mainly southern England.

name: Egeria densa
tip: Bright green waterweed with leaves in whorls of four to six and relatively large white three-petalled flowers above the surface. Introduced in ponds and canals.

name: Elodea callitrichoides
tip: Narrow waterweed like Canadian Waterweed but with thinner, slightly twisted leaves. Specialist check needed; very rare, introduced in canals.

name: Hydrilla verticillata
tip: Submerged, whorled waterweed with leaves in fours to eight with sharp spiny-toothed edges. Native only in Esthwaite Water, Cumbria; also introduced elsewhere.

name: Hydrocharis morsus-ranae
tip: Floating plant with small round heart-shaped leaves and three-petalled white flowers with yellow centres. Found in still lowland ditches and ponds in England and Wales.

name: Najas flexilis
tip: Slender submerged annual with narrow, finely toothed leaves in small tufts. Rare, in lochs in Scotland and in Ireland.

name: Najas marina
tip: Brittle submerged plant with broad, spiny-toothed leaves. Very rare, in Norfolk Broads and nearby waters.

name: Stratiotes aloides
tip: Floating rosette of stiff, spiky, pineapple-like leaves; white flowers rise above the water. Native in the Norfolk Broads and Yorkshire, otherwise introduced.

name: Vallisneria spiralis
tip: Submerged plant with long, ribbon-like leaves. Female flowers float on a spiral stalk. Naturalised in warm-water areas such as canals and warm outflows.

name: Hymenophyllum tunbrigense
tip: Tiny translucent, moss-like fern with fronds one cell thick and wedge-shaped, toothed lobes. Found on damp shady rocks, trees and rock walls in the west, and Tunbridge Wells.

name: Hymenophyllum wilsonii
tip: Tiny translucent, filmy fern with fronds one cell thick, forming mats. Distinguished from Tunbridge Filmy-fern by narrower, entire-edged lobes. Found on damp shady rocks and bark in the west.

name: Trichomanes speciosum
tip: Delicate translucent fern with leathery, dark green, divided fronds creeping from a hairy rhizome. Very rare in damp, shaded ravine rocks in Ireland and western Britain.

name: Hypericum canadense
tip: Slender plant with narrow stalkless leaves and tiny pale yellow flowers with five petals. Rare native of western Ireland on damp sandy or peaty ground.

name: Hypericum elodes
tip: Densely grey-hairy plant of boggy ground with rounded woolly leaves and pale yellow flowers. The soft felty look separates it from other St John's-worts.

name: Hypericum forrestii
tip: Garden shrub with leafy arching stems and large golden flowers with many stamens. Occasionally escapes; confirm species against other cultivated shrubby St John's-worts.

name: Hypericum linariifolium
tip: Narrow, almost linear leaves with rolled edges and small yellow flowers. Very rare native of rocky heath in Devon and Cornwall, scarce elsewhere.

name: Hypericum montanum
tip: Pale lemon flowers and stalkless leaves with black dots on the margins only. Hairy upper stem. Local on limestone and calcareous scrub in England and Wales.

name: Hypericum nummularium
tip: Low rock-garden plant with small rounded greyish leaves and few yellow flowers. Rarely seen outside gardens; check against other trailing garden St John's-worts.

name: Hypericum olympicum
tip: Low, greyish rock-garden shrublet with narrow blue-green leaves and large lemon-yellow flowers. Cultivated and only an occasional garden escape.

name: Hypericum pseudohenryi
tip: Garden shrub with large, bright golden flowers and many stamens, close to other cultivated shrubby kinds. Rare outside gardens; identification needs checking.

name: Hypericum undulatum
tip: Leaves with wavy margins, stems with narrow wings, and small pale yellow flowers marked red. Rare plant of damp acid ground in Cornwall, Devon and Wales.

name: Hypericum xylosteifolium
tip: Evergreen-ish shrub with oval, rather soft leaves and large bright yellow flowers followed by red fruit. Occasionally persists near gardens and in hedges.

name: Aristea ecklonii
tip: South African garden plant with narrow sword-shaped leaves and spikes of small blue flowers. Occasional garden escape or throw-out in mild areas.

name: Chasmanthe bicolor
tip: Tall sword-shaped leaves and a one-sided spike of tubular orange-red flowers in spring. Naturalised on mild coasts, mainly in south-west England and the Isles of Scilly.

name: Crocosmia masoniorum
tip: Tall plant with pleated sword leaves and large orange flowers held facing outwards in a zigzag spike. Larger flowers than common montbretia; garden escape.

name: Crocosmia paniculata
tip: Stiff, pleated, sword-like leaves and dense orange-red flowers on branched spikes. Taller and more upright than common montbretia; occasional garden escape.

name: Crocosmia pottsii
tip: Pleated sword-shaped leaves and a branched spike of orange-yellow flowers. Parent of common montbretia; naturalised in damp ground, mostly in western areas.

name: Crocus ancyrensis
tip: Small, bright yellow crocus with a narrow white stripe down the leaf, flowering very early. Occasionally naturalised in grass near gardens.

name: Crocus biflorus
tip: Small crocus with white or lilac flowers, often feathered purple outside and yellow throat. Naturalised in grassland and churchyards; the name reflects old garden use.

name: Crocus chrysanthus
tip: Small early crocus with honey-scented golden-yellow flowers, often marked bronze outside. Naturalised in lawns and grassy banks near gardens.

name: Crocus kotschyanus
tip: Autumn-flowering crocus with lilac flowers and a yellow throat, appearing with or before narrow leaves. Occasional garden escape in grass.

name: Crocus neapolitanus
tip: Spring crocus with large white to purple flowers and a single white stripe on the leaf. Naturalised in meadows and parkland, often confused with other spring crocuses.

name: Crocus nudiflorus
tip: Large purple crocus appearing in autumn without leaves, which come later. Not to be confused with the colchicum. Local in a few English grasslands.

name: Crocus speciosus
tip: Autumn crocus with blue-violet flowers that have darker veins, appearing before the leaves. Naturalised locally in lawns and grass near gardens.

name: Gladiolus communis
tip: Tall plant with sword-shaped leaves and spikes of bright magenta flowers. Garden escape; naturalised locally in the south-west, especially Cornwall and Scilly.

name: Gladiolus illyricus
tip: Slim spike of rich purple-pink flowers among bracken and heath. Very rare native, found only in the New Forest and nearby parts of Hampshire and Dorset.

name: Iris germanica
tip: Large blue-purple flowers with a fuzzy yellow beard on each lower petal, and stout fans of sword leaves. Garden plant surviving on tips and verges.

name: Iris laevigata
tip: Blue-purple flowers with flattened, beardless petals and broad pale-green leaves. Garden pond plant that sometimes persists beside water.

name: Iris latifolia
tip: Large violet-blue flowers with a yellow patch on each lower petal and broad grassy leaves. Cultivated garden plant; occasional escape.

name: Iris orientalis
tip: White flowers marked with a yellow blotch on the lower petals, plus tall stems and narrow grey-green leaves. Rare garden relic.

name: Iris sibirica
tip: Slender stems carry several blue-violet beardless flowers above very narrow grassy leaves. Garden plant occasionally persisting in damp grass near gardens.

name: Iris spuria
tip: Tall iris of grassland with narrow leaves and lilac-blue flowers with a small yellow-veined blotch. Rare garden escape or relic.

name: Iris tuberosa
tip: Odd green and black-purple flowers with hooded form, on short stems with square-sectioned leaves. Naturalised in a few spots in southern England.

name: Iris versicolor
tip: Violet-purple flowers veined darker with a yellow centre, rather like Yellow Iris in leaf shape. Damp-ground garden escape, uncommon.

name: Ixia campanulata
tip: Slender wiry stems carry a spike of reddish bell-shaped flowers over thin sword leaves. Rare garden plant, uncertain outside cultivation.

name: Libertia formosa
tip: Clump of tough, narrow evergreen leaves with sprays of three-petalled white flowers on stiff stems. Garden plant occasionally found on mild-area waste ground.

name: Romulea columnae
tip: Tiny crocus-like plant with lilac, white-throated flowers opening only in sun. Very rare coastal turf in Cornwall, Devon and the Channel Islands.

name: Schizostylis coccinea
tip: Spikes of bright crimson-pink star-shaped flowers in autumn over narrow sword leaves. Garden plant occasionally escaping into damp, sheltered ground.

name: Sisyrinchium bermudiana
tip: Flat, winged stems with narrow leaves and violet-blue flowers with a yellow eye. Rare native in western Ireland near lakes and damp pasture.

name: Sisyrinchium californicum
tip: Narrow irislike leaves and yellow six-petalled flowers on flat stems. Garden plant, naturalised locally in damp grassland in western Britain and Ireland.

name: Sisyrinchium montanum
tip: Flattened winged stems and narrow grey-green leaves, with violet-blue flowers with a yellow eye. Naturalised in damp grass and roadsides, especially northern Britain.

name: Watsonia borbonica
tip: Tall spikes of tubular pinkish-orange flowers over stiff, sword-shaped leaves. Garden plant of mild areas, rarely escaping.

name: Isoetes echinospora
tip: Tuft of stiff, quill-like leaves under water, no flowers; spiny spores need microscope checks. Rare in soft-water lakes and pools in Wales, Scotland and Ireland.

name: Isoetes histrix
tip: Tiny tuft of short, bristle-like leaves on damp ground, no flowers, which disappears in summer. Very rare, known from Cornwall and the Channel Islands.

name: Isoetes lacustris
tip: Rosette of stiff, dark-green quill leaves on the bed of clear mountain lakes, no flowers. Local in upland Wales, Scotland, Ireland and the Lake District.

name: Juglans nigra
tip: Large tree with long leaves of many toothed leaflets, deeply furrowed dark bark and round green fruits. Planted in parks; sometimes self-sown.

name: Pterocarya fraxinifolia
tip: Big tree with long ridged leaf-stalks bearing many leaflets, and hanging chains of winged green fruits. Planted in parks, often spreading by suckers.

name: Juncus acutus
tip: Very stout, sharply spine-tipped grey-green rush forming tussocks. Local on coastal dunes and damp slacks in Wales, south and east England and Ireland.

name: Juncus alpinoarticulatus
tip: Slender creeping rush with dark brown flower clusters at stem ends, flowering heads rather loose. Rare plant of wet upland flushes in northern Britain; a specialist should confirm.

name: Juncus balticus
tip: Rhizomatous rush with stems spaced out along the rhizome and a lateral brown flower cluster. Coastal dune slacks in Scotland, northern England, Wales and Ireland.

name: Juncus biglumis
tip: Short rush with only two dark flowers in a terminal head and a leaf-like bract below. Rare on wet mountain flushes in the Scottish Highlands.

name: Juncus capitatus
tip: Tiny tufted annual rush with a few small reddish-brown flower heads. Very rare, on damp bare ground, mainly Cornwall, Devon and Channel Islands.

name: Juncus castaneus
tip: Rush with large chestnut-brown flower heads at stem tops, with stems and leaves flat. Rare in wet mountain flushes in the central Scottish Highlands.

name: Juncus compressus
tip: Flattened wiry stems, unlike thread-like ones of the commoner rushes, and round-fruited loose brown heads. Scarce on damp grass in south and east England.

name: Juncus dudleyi
tip: Slender rush resembling Tuberculate relatives, with clear ear-like auricles on the leaf sheath. Introduced from North America and very local; a specialist should confirm.

name: Juncus filiformis
tip: Very slender rush with thread-like stems, and flower clusters appearing on the side of the stem. Rare in upland Britain, by lakes and streams in Scotland.

name: Juncus foliosus
tip: Perennial rush with flattened leaves and star-like clusters of pointed fruits. Easily confused with Jointed Rush; a specialist is needed to confirm. Mainly in western areas.

name: Juncus maritimus
tip: Tall, stiff grey-green rush with sharp spine-tipped stems, and a loose branched flower cluster below the tip. Common in salt marshes and coastal flats.

name: Juncus planifolius
tip: Rush with flat, grass-like leaves and small round heads of green-brown flowers. Introduced from Australasia; rare, mostly in damp turf and lawns.

name: Juncus pygmaeus
tip: Tiny tufted annual rush with minute yellow-brown flowers and awl-shaped leaves. Very rare, on damp bare ground on the Lizard in Cornwall.

name: Juncus ranarius
tip: Small, branched, spreading annual, with tiny flower clusters at branch tips. Can be mistaken for Toad Rush; a close look at fruits is needed. Introduced.

name: Juncus subnodulosus
tip: Tall rush with rough, ridged stems, and blunt flowers in loose clusters. Similar to Sharp-flowered Rush; found in fens and wet meadows, mainly lowland England and Ireland.

name: Juncus trifidus
tip: Dense wiry tufts with stiff stems that bear three leaf-like bracts under a small flower cluster. Upland rush of Scottish mountain tops and rocky ledges.

name: Juncus triglumis
tip: Small rush with three pale to brown flowers in a terminal cluster, with pointed bracts. Local in wet mountain flushes in the Scottish Highlands and northern Ireland.

name: Juncus xiphioides
tip: Flat, sword-like leaves arranged like an iris, with long creeping stems and branched flower clusters. Introduced garden plant, rarely spreads in wet ground.

name: Luzula arcuata
tip: Small tufted wood-rush, with arching nodding dark clusters on thin stems. Only on high Scottish mountain tops, in bare stony ground and snowbeds.

name: Luzula forsteri
tip: Slender wood-rush with a few hairs on leaf edges and sparse branched clusters of small brown flowers. Local in woods in south and east England.

name: Luzula luzuloides
tip: Larger tufts with hairy leaves and loose clusters of pale whitish flowers. Introduced, naturalised in woods and on acidic ground in a few places.

name: Luzula pallescens
tip: Hairy-edged grassy leaves and compact heads of small shiny brown flowers. Introduced from Europe, spreading in lawns and woodland edges, especially in the south and east.

name: Luzula spicata
tip: Short wood-rush with a nodding spike-like head of dark brown flowers, and leaves with few hairs. Mountain rush of Scottish uplands and Lake District fells.

name: Laurus nobilis
tip: Evergreen shrub or tree with glossy, aromatic, pointed oval leaves and small yellow-green flower clusters. Often planted; self-sown seedlings found near gardens.

name: Pinguicula grandiflora
tip: Sticky yellow-green leaf rosette with big violet flowers on a long stalk. Local in damp rocks and bogs in south-west Ireland.

name: Pinguicula lusitanica
tip: Pale lilac small flowers with yellow throat above flat, sticky greenish rosette. Local in wet heath and bog in western Scotland, Wales, south-west England and Ireland.

name: Utricularia australis
tip: Floating aquatic with finely cut leaves bearing small bladders and yellow flowers on a stem above water. Similar to Greater Bladderwort; specialist check needed.

name: Utricularia bremii
tip: Floating aquatic with finely divided leaves and small yellow flowers; a close relative of other bladderworts. Extremely rare and needs specialist confirmation.

name: Utricularia intermedia
tip: Aquatic with two kinds of shoots: green ones with bristly forked leaves, and pale ones carrying bladders buried in peat. Pale yellow flowers; in bog pools.

name: Utricularia minor
tip: Small aquatic with fine bladder-bearing leaves and pale yellow flowers with a flattish lip. Rarely flowers; found in peaty pools and ditches.

name: Utricularia ochroleuca
tip: Aquatic with pale buried bladder shoots and pale yellow flowers, rarely produced. Very local in peaty pools in north-west Scotland and western Ireland.

name: Utricularia stygia
tip: Aquatic bladderwort with fine leaves and pale yellow flowers, rarely seen in bloom. Very local in Scotland and western Ireland; a specialist is needed to confirm.

name: Utricularia vulgaris
tip: Floating aquatic with feathery leaves bearing dark bladders and a spike of bright yellow flowers held above the water. Local in clean ditches and ponds.

name: Erythronium dens-canis
tip: Nodding pink flower with swept-back petals and blotched leaves in pairs, with no true stem. Naturalised locally in woods and grassy places.

name: Fritillaria meleagris
tip: Nodding bell with chequered purple or white petals on a slender stem with narrow grey-green leaves. Local in old damp meadows in southern and central England.

name: Gagea bohemica
tip: Small plant with yellow flowers having greenish backs and just two narrow leaves; one basal leaf only. Extremely rare, in Radnorshire and Pembrokeshire in Wales.
